..*In those days, after that tribulation, the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, And the stars of heaven shall fall, and the powers that are in heaven shall be shaken. And then shall they see the Son of man coming in the clouds with great power and glory. And then shall he send his angels, and shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from the uttermost part of the earth to the uttermost part of heaven.*

In those days. AFTER the tribulation. The return. The rapture. The promise of eternal life given in the day of redemption, the Great Day of the Lord come at last! Amen.

teachings.title: Revealed from heaven in flaming fire
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: 2 Thessalonians 1 lines up with Matthew 24 and Revelation 6: out of tribulation Christ is revealed from heaven, gathers the living and resurrected saints, and takes vengeance on the disobedient.
teachings.text:
In 2nd Thessalonians, Paul, Silvanus and Timothy writing unto the church in Thessalonica to encourage them in their faith, through all the persecution and tribulations they endure.

These early believers, who accepted and obeyed the Gospel of faith towards Jesus, as given by the Apostle and evangelists, were beset by persecution, tribulation by man, suffering for God. To bolster their spirit, Paul writes to remind them that patience, enduring troubles is a blessing, a manifestation of the righteous judgement of God, that they may be counted worthy of the kingdom of Heaven, to which we as believers belong.

That we have the promise from God that all those unrighteous who trouble us as believers will be recompensed for what they've done, on that great and terrible day, when Jesus returns.

Tying in to the timing of that day to the preaching of Jesus in Matthew 24, we see the concurrency of events, and just as Revelation 6, a slightly different perspective of the same events.

Out of tribulation, the Lord Jesus will be revealed from Heaven with His mighty angels, taking vengeance with flaming fire on them that know not God and are disobedient to the Gospel of Jesus Christ our Lord.

Again, we see Jesus returning as he ascended, in the clouds but with a noise and sight to behold by all the world, and the gathering of the resurrected believers and those saints alive, saved from tribulation by His return:

**Matthew 24:30-31**
*And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.*

**Revelation 1:7** *Behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him, and they also which pierced him: and all kindreds of the earth shall wail because of him. Even so, Amen.*

**1 Thessalonians 4:16-17**
*For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord.*

teachings.title: Let no man deceive you: these come first
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: Scripture says the falling away and the revealing of the man of sin come before the day of the Lord, so believers are to watch the signs as the fig tree instead of trusting the pre-trib imminence teaching.
teachings.text:
And so we see the timing of things leading us to this day, the clock already ticking towards this inevitable event.

But the patience of the saints is tried, today just as it was in the first century. And as Jesus warned the disciples regarding the timing of the end of the world, "*Take heed that no man deceive you,*" so to does Paul echo Christ's sentiment;

*Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition; Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped; so that he as God sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God.*

No man knoweth the day or hour that these things will come to pass, but the false teachings of the imminency of Christ's return given by the pre-trib dispensationalists ignores the signs of the times the Bible tells us to watch for. That once certain events come to pass, we may know the day of the Lord is at hand.

Let no man deceive you. These things happen first. This is consistently taught in scripture regarding end times Bible prophecy. That we are as the watchmen, sober and vigilant that we may recognize the times as they come.

**Matthew 24:32-33**
*Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh: So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.*

We know there will be a falling away, a great apostasy. We know that iniquity shall abound, worse and worse. We know that the man of sin will be revealed. That he should conquer the world, set himself up as God and his mark be issued, that all who do not believe on Christ will worship him as God.

*And then shall that Wicked be revealed, whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming:*

*Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders, And with all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish; because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved. And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie: That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.*

And the Bible says that there will come at the midpoint of the Great Tribulation, Daniel's prophecy of the abomination of desolation, in the midst of Jerusalem. Jesus says those who have eyes to see will understand, and that this signals the coming of the Lord.

But to those who are not saved, to the perishing, Jesus will come upon them as a thief in the night.

*But as the days of Noah were, so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.*

*For as in the days that were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away; so shall also the coming of the Son of man be.*

And so, Jesus encourages us to be vigilant that we may know the signs and prepare;

*Watch therefore: for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come. But know this, that if the goodman of the house had known in what watch the thief would come, he would have watched, and would not have suffered his house to be broken up. Therefore be ye also ready: for in such an hour as ye think not the Son of man cometh.*

*Who then is a faithful and wise servant, whom his lord hath made ruler over his household, to give them meat in due season?*

*Blessed is that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find so doing.*

*Verily I say unto you, That he shall make him ruler over all his goods.*

*But and if that evil servant shall say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming; And shall begin to smite his fellowservants, and to eat and drink with the drunken; The lord of that servant shall come in a day when he looketh not for him, and in an hour that he is not aware of,*

teachings.title: This generation shall not pass
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: This generation means the generation that sees the signs, not merely the first century or the Jews, and Christ's word that their house is left desolate shows God's wrath on the unbelieving Jews.
teachings.text:
As for the verse following the parable of the fig tree, **Matthew 24:34**, which gives so many trouble;

*Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass, till all these things be fulfilled.*

Jesus has just laid out future prophecy, written to us as much as to the Apostles to whom he preached. (Again, the false doctrine of dispensationalism teaches that this is directed at the Jews, who weren't present and who Jesus refers to as "they," as others, while referring to we, ye the believers, making their interpretation nonsensical.)

So Jesus is preaching of the future generation, present at the time of these signs. Who are reading the times as one could read the fig tree in its due season. This is that generation, which we may be under, or our great grandchildren for that matter. But once the timing of things is made clear to those keeping watch, prepared for the master's return, that generation will not pass until all those things be revealed.

There is dual fulfillment as well, obviously, that the generation of 1st century believers would live to see the destruction in 70AD, but that is not the context of what's given, and those who seek to make it about that have to do contortions to make it fit their doctrine, that the end times is entirely about the Jews.

"God is not finished with the Jews!" Really? In the chapter previous, **Matthew 23**, just before Jesus leaving the temple at the start of this private discourse on Olivet to the apostles, Christ makes it known in no uncertain terms:

*O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not! Behold, your house is left unto you desolate. For I say unto you, Ye shall not see me henceforth, till ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord.*

He was through preaching to them that believed not and rejected Him as they rejected the prophets that came before Him. God's wrath abides upon them to the uttermost. From that day forth, an accursed and wicked generation of men.

But they are correct about one thing, God isn't through with them yet. And the Days of Vengeance they who remain, that Synagogue of Satan, will be utterly destroyed.

teachings.title: The false hope of escaping tribulation
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: All who live godly will suffer, and the Left Behind hope of a secret rapture before the worst is a snare belonging to lukewarm churches and drunken watchmen.
teachings.text:
There's obviously more to say on this, the subject of end times prophecy is exhaustive and deep. But the fundamentals, the tribulations we will suffer, now and in the Great Tribulation, must be. All who live Godly will be persecuted for His name's sake. Jesus came to divide, even from family, who will hate us, and give us up to judgement of the wicked.

The false hope that we will not be made to suffer for the faith, that we will be secretly raptured ala Left Behind, and not be present for the worst of it, is part and parcel with the lukewarm churches, the drunken watchmen, those who win no souls, gather no wheat for the harvest, who sit in laser light fun-centers, being told faithless affirmations by vipers who deny the power of Christ's blood...that false hope to avoid troubles is a snare and a stumbling block. And to them the end truly will come as a thief in the night.

teachings.title: He that endureth: saved out of tribulation
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: Jesus' promise that those who endure will be saved is, in context, physical deliverance of the saints from the tribulation at His coming, not a condition of spiritual salvation.
teachings.text:
Continuing, Jesus says, then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, to be killed, hated for His name's sake.

Although He is speaking to the disciples of their fate, remember that the context of this preaching is of the end times. Most Biblical prophecy has at least a double meaning, dual fulfillment. What many do is take the single application they want from it, out of the larger context to make the verses fit their preferred meaning.

And so, like with the beginning of sorrows we see the persecution of the saints spoken of by Jesus reflected in Revelation 6:9 and the souls of them that were slain for the word of God.

Jesus gives detail to the earthly experience of the martyrs and saints' persecution, where John gives us the Heavenly POV.

Christians will be hated by the world, even by family. False prophets will lead pogroms against us. Sin will run rampant, and many believers will fall away to avoid persecution, still saved but their love waxed cold. But we are encouraged to persevere through this tribulation, for in the end Jesus coming on the day of the Lord will save us from it.

This is, in context, physical salvation from the tribulation, not spiritual salvation. The false doctrine that claims only those who persevere are saved in a spiritual sense contradicts the context given.

teachings.title: The last days and the Olivet question
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: We have been in the last days since the Ascension, and the temple's destruction is a separate prophecy from Christ's coming, which dispensationalists and preterists both mix up.
teachings.text:
The idea of dual fulfillment, and a definitions of what constitutes the end times has long been a contentious point.

**2 Peter 3** addresses this, that even in that first century:

*Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts,And saying, Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation.*

Peter goes on to warn against those casting doubts regarding the kingdom to come and the resurrection, who took prophecy as singular, and allegorical, and used that point of view to undermine the faith in the Kingdom promised us in Christ.

According to **Colossians 1:5-6**, the gospel has been preached to the whole world, even at that time. And as Peter notes, and is referenced in other Epistles, the last days have come following the Ascension of Christ. We are living in the end times, and have for 2,000 years if the calendar is to be believed.

What triggered Jesus' discourse was the Apostles wondering at the buildings of the temple, and Jesus prophesying that it would be destroyed, not one stone left upon another. It is after this that they privately ask Jesus, "*Tell us, when shall these things be? and what shall be the sign of thy coming, and of the end of the world*?"

Dispensationalists and others will take the destruction of the temple and add it to the prophecy that follows regarding His second coming and the end of the world, when it is a separate prophecy that spurred the broader discussion.

Preterists will take the same approach, but say all things were fulfilled in 70AD with its destruction.

But fundamentalists, reading in the spirit can see the order of how this is presented in Matthew 24. Rightly dividing the word of God.

teachings.title: Immediately after the tribulation of those days
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: Matthew 24 puts the great tribulation first and Christ's visible coming and the gathering of the saints immediately after it, with the darkened sun and moon of Revelation 6, refuting the pre-trib rapture.
teachings.text:
So continuing on with His prophecy, Jesus talks about "they" and "them" in Judea, fleeing what is called the "days of vengeance" in the parallel passage in Luke 21. It appears throughout the matching Gospel accounts that this is not referring to Christian believers but the Jews, as it's consistently othering pronouns. However, when talking about travel on the sabbath, He switches to "ye," the personal form, indicating the disciples and believers. I lean towards that the days of vengeance reflect both what happens to the unbelieving Jews in 70AD as well as their destruction in the end times of revelation, both. Regardless, it was also a time of tribulation for believers in Judea, and would be again when the beast turns his armies to betray the Jews, and take up his spot in Jerusalem, proclaiming himself God.

Jesus tells us this is the days of great tribulation, where He has not returned as yet, and the resurrection and rapture has yet to take place. Dispensationalists insist the Great Tribulation occurs after a secret second coming and rapture, despite these clear verses giving the order of things.

*For then shall be great tribulation, such as was not since the beginning of the world to this time, no, nor ever shall be. And except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elect's sake those days shall be shortened.*

Again we see that this will be worse than anything that has ever occurred, and we have witnessed world wars with the deaths of tens of millions. The starvation and execution of tens of millions under Stalin and Mao. Greater than that. It's gonna be bad, and believers alive during this time will be mercifully saved by the shortening the time, 3 and a half years rather than 7. It is at this midpoint that the abomination of desolation occurs, whatever that may finally look like. We the believers will recognize it, but it has yet to come.

Jesus warns that during this time many false Christs and reports of His return will be made, but not be be fooled. That His coming will be like lightening that fills the entire sky. That it will be with a shout that is heard throughout the world. Every eye will see and ear hear His presence in the sky. He won't be in a hidden place, a cave, the wilderness. That His presence in the heavens will be like a carcass surrounded by carrion birds, as eagles, because He will be surrounded by the hosts of the saints caught up with Him in the clouds. (Rapture is just a Latin term meaning 'caught up,' for those special boys who say 'acctuuuually, rapture doesn't appear in the Bible!")

Now with these caveats, Jesus begins to reveal what will happen on the Day of the Lord.

*Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken.*

Note the timing is AFTER THE TRIBULATION. Not before. Pre-trib rapture heresy BTFO with one verse, straight from Christ's mouth.

We see the parallel in **Revelation 6**:

*And I beheld when he had opened the sixth seal, and, lo, there was a great earthquake; and the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the moon became as blood; And the stars of heaven fell unto the earth, even as a fig tree casteth her untimely figs, when she is shaken of a mighty wind. And the heaven departed as a scroll when it is rolled together; and every mountain and island were moved out of their places.*

The sun and moon darkened is a common theme throughout the end times Bible prophecy, it is the common feature of all mentions of the Day of the Lord, second coming. It is an unmistakable sign that cannot be faked, and has not taken place in history of creation. Those claiming that the prophecy is past, that the resurrection has already taken place, that Jesus has already returned and we are in the millennium now, or had been, are all dependant on ignoring this incredible occurrence.

teachings.title: The falling away first, and the corrupt versions
teachings.theme: After the tribulation, before the wrath
teachings.summary: 2 Thessalonians 2 says the falling away and the man of sin come before the day of Christ, and modern versions that turn the falling away into rebellion and lawlessness set believers up to be seen as the rebels against the antichrist.
teachings.text:
Just touching on this theme: The push for false Christianity that places salvation under the law, not under grace, the Noahide false religion, Hebrew Roots, Lordship/Repenting of sin, Judaizing, etc...is meant to bring about the falling away of believers, and pave the way for the antichrist and his false claim of being Jesus, returned.

In **2 Thessalonians 2**, we see the order and type of things to come:

*Now we beseech you, brethren, by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him,*

*2 That ye be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled, neither by spirit, nor by word, nor by letter as from us, as that the day of Christ is at hand.*

*3 Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition;*

*4 Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped; so that he as God sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God.*

*5 Remember ye not, that, when I was yet with you, I told you these things?*

*6 And now ye know what withholdeth that he might be revealed in his time.*

Scripture says don't be deceived, no matter who you hear it from, the day of the Lord **will not** come until there is a falling away of believers, the antichrist revealed, *the man of sin* who will take the place of Jesus, naming himself God.

But the eschatology of false Christianity says what? That first Jesus comes, and the rapture either a "secret rapture" of the dispensationalist crowd, or a "symbolic event," not literal. Note, this all occurs in their false timeline before the rise of the antichrist, Great Tribulation, etc.

Now look at the same chapter and verse in the non-inspired version:

2 Thessalonians 2
New International Version

The Man of Lawlessness

Concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our being gathered to him, we ask you, brothers and sisters, 2 not to become easily unsettled or alarmed by the teaching allegedly from us—whether by a prophecy or by word of mouth or by letter—asserting that the day of the Lord has already come. 3 Don’t let anyone deceive you in any way, for that day will not come until the rebellion occurs and the man of lawlessness is revealed, the man doomed to destruction. 4 He will oppose and will exalt himself over everything that is called God or is worshiped, so that he sets himself up in God’s temple, proclaiming himself to be God. 5 Don’t you remember that when I was with you I used to tell you these things? 6 And now you know what is holding him back, so that he may be revealed at the proper time. 7 For the secret power of lawlessness is already at work; but the one who now holds it back will continue to do so till he is taken out of the way. 8 And then the lawless one will be revealed, whom the Lord Jesus will overthrow with the breath of his mouth and destroy by the splendor of his coming.

Notice the heading, and throughout it talks about lawlessness, not sin. The falling away becomes "rebellion."

So if you were expecting the Second Coming first, before the Tribulation, and paint the picture of those who oppose the antichrist as lawless and rebellious, you can see how the stage is set for these false versions to fool all but the very elect. That believers who oppose the antichrist, who they will hail as Christ, and our rebelling against him, being against the law as a means of salvation, etc, we would be seen as the "bad guys" by these false believers under the beast's delusion, and the fraudulent Bible versions used to reinforce it to persecute those of us under grace.

This change from sin and falling away to "rebellion and lawlessness" is in the ESV, NASB, RSV.

*Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the LORD God had made. And he said unto the woman, Yea, hath God said..?*

teachings.title: The day of the Lord in Zechariah 14
teachings.summary: Just before Christ returns with His saints, the Antichrist's nations take Jerusalem, then the Lord splits the Mount of Olives, pours out wrath and reigns from Zion.
teachings.text:
*Behold, the day of the Lord cometh, and thy spoil shall be divided in the midst of thee.*

End-times prophecy is given, the day of the Lord is assured. But just before His return, Jerusalem will be set upon by an army of all nations. The Days of Vengeance, led by the Antichrist. The city taken, trampled underfoot by the nations. The Gentiles.

**Luke 21:22-24**
*For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled. But woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck, in those days! for there shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon this people. And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.*

Jesus returns with His saints, and splits the Mt of Olives in two. A valley running East to West. The site of Christ's Olivet Discourse.

The unnatural light describes the earth illuminated by the glory of Jesus. The sun and moon darkened. The stars not giving their light, as described also in **Matthew 24**.

A great curse is upon those that rose up. A consumption without death. Similar to the sores and suffering in the wrath described in **Revelation**.

And the rivers of living water, the Spirit of God, will flow out to the ends of the earth.

And the nations during the millennium will come up to the feasts in Jerusalem, the prophet says, and if any do not, they will have rain held back.

Some interpretations hold that the OT feasts will be honored in the NT Kingdom. But as we discussed in the study of Ezekiel, OT prophecy still retained elements of the Old Covenant, while the Revelation of Jesus Christ in the New Testament changes things slightly to better reflect that new covenant made necessary by the failure of the Jews.

*Yea, every pot in Jerusalem and in Judah shall be holiness*. Common pots and pans for normal cooking will be as holy as the temple's vessels. I think this is symbolic of the glorified saints being sanctified, that even common is holy. The *no more the Canaanite in the house of the Lord of hosts* indicating no more heathen, no more tares in the wheat.

But the Lord will reign from Zion. Amen

teachings.title: Babylon is fallen, is fallen
teachings.summary: As Babylon's fall signalled the end of Judah's captivity, the fall of Babylon in Revelation signals that God's wrath is nearing its end and Armageddon is near.
teachings.text:
Here in **Isaiah 21**, the prophet has multiple visions of the various nations that are in the region, just as the previous chapters.

It begins with another foretelling of the destruction of Babylon, by the Persians and Medes. *Go up, O Elam: besiege, O Media*...Elam referring to the Persians, Media of Medes, and their preferred method of chariots, asses and camels.

This prophecy is again taking place at a time where the greatness of the Babylonian empire had yet to occur, let alone her end at the hands of Cyrus and the Medo-Persian Empire.

But its prophesied destruction served as a hope to those of Judah during the eventual 70yr captivity. That the corn of the Lord's threshing floor, those saved by faith having been separated from the chaff by the threshing, by tribulation, will know when this happens, when the treachery and spoils come against Babylon by Cyrus, their time of captivity would be near its end.

In much the same way, we see the similarities to **Revelation 18:1-2**;

*And after these things I saw another angel come down from heaven, having great power; and the earth was lightened with his glory.And he cried mightily with a strong voice, saying, Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and is become the habitation of devils, and the hold of every foul spirit, and a cage of every unclean and hateful bird.*

Here in Isaiah, it is the watchman of his vision;

*And he answered and said, Babylon is fallen, is fallen; and all the graven images of her gods he hath broken unto the ground.*

For those in the 1,260 days of the wrath, the fall of Babylon is a sign that the wrath of God is nearing its end, and the battle of Armageddon drawing nigh. The Millennial Reign set to begin.

teachings.title: The burden of Babylon and the day of His wrath
teachings.summary: Isaiah's prophecy against Babylon has a dual fulfillment, in the fall of the Babylonian empire and in the destruction of the spirit of Babylon in the wrath to come, when no silver or gold can deliver.
teachings.text:
The prophecy of Isaiah against Babylon, they the day of the Lord is at hand, clearly has dual fulfillment. It speaks not only of the destruction of Babylonian empire, which had only risen to prominence in the days of Isaiah, but that same spirit of Babylon which will be destroyed in the wrath to come.

...*cruel both with wrath and fierce anger, to lay the land desolate: and he shall destroy the sinners thereof out of it. For the stars of heaven and the constellations thereof shall not give their light: the sun shall be darkened in his going forth, and the moon shall not cause her light to shine. And I will punish the world for their evil, and the wicked for their iniquity; and I will cause the arrogancy of the proud to cease, and will lay low the haughtiness of the terrible.*

**Malachi 3:2**
*But who may abide the day of his coming? and who shall stand when he appeareth?*

And as Isaiah preached, the Persians and Medes had no regard for gold and silver, the Lord's judgment can't be swayed either.

**Zephaniah 1:18**
*Neither their silver nor their gold shall be able to deliver them in the day of the Lord's wrath; but the whole land shall be devoured by the fire of his jealousy: for he shall make even a speedy riddance of all them that dwell in the land.*

**Revelation 6:17**
*For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand?*

teachings.title: Cease ye from man
teachings.summary: Proud men who trust in men, riches and idols will hide in the rocks from the wrath of the Lamb, while the meek inherit the earth.
teachings.text:
**Isaiah 2** continues the clear teaching of the Lord, and the futility of those who trust in men, things of men like riches and chariots, and especially idols made with hands.

We know in Christ's wrath, on that great and terrible day, that the proud and haughty men will be brought low, and attempt to hide from His wrath:

**Revelation 6:15-17**
*And the kings of the earth, and the great men, and the rich men, and the chief captains, and the mighty men, and every bondman, and every free man, hid themselves in the dens and in the rocks of the mountains; And said to the mountains and rocks, Fall on us, and hide us from the face of him that sitteth on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb: For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand?*

They will be brought low and flee to the mountains and the caves and their bunkers and pray for the rocks to cover them, and there will be nowhere left to hide.

But the meek shall inherit the earth. The humble and poor of spirit are blessed by God through Christ.

And all nations will be under the King of kings. And be taught by Him, and walk in His paths.

Knowing this, Isaiah appeals to Judah, the house of Jacob. Why trust they in men? In the power of other nations to save them? In idols of gods made by hands? *Cease ye from man, whose breath is in his nostrils: for wherein is he to be accounted of?*

*O house of Jacob, come ye, and let us walk in the light of the Lord.*

Disobedient Judah, having the oracles of God, knowing the redemption of Christ to come, and the day of judgment to follow, and yet still they trusted in vanity. As so many do today.

teachings.title: Jerusalem's desolation and the day of the Lord
teachings.summary: As God slew Jerusalem without pity, so in the day of the Lord none of the nations will escape His anger except His servants carried away to His kingdom.
teachings.text:
**Lamentations** chapter 2, like chapter 1 and 4, is 22 verses, because these poems are written in an acrostic format, where each verse is started by a letter in the alphabet, in this case the 22 letters of the Hebrew language. Verse 3, as we will see, is 66 verses, because it uses the same format, but repeats 3 lines per letter.

It is interesting that God's poetry loses nothing in their beauty being translated to English, the poems and Psalms not relying on a meter or rhyme.

And of course, these poems of lamentation are Jeremiah's weeping over the destruction of Judah by the Babylonians, but clearly by the hand of God.

The first chapter describing Jerusalem as a widow and an adulterous, left desolate and friendless. The second, a daughter left without hope, covered in a cloud in his anger, and cast down from previous highs, brought low by His wrath.

The prophet describes how the Lord has torn down their habitations, their walls and strongholds, their temple and altars, kings and princes, priests and prophets. Taken everything from them. That their children beg for wine (juice) and bread in hunger.

*The Lord was as an enemy*, He bent his bow against them as an enemy. His wrath was upon them as He violently took away their Tabernacle, cast off the altar, ended the law, the sacrifices...taken from them everything. Only a remnant saved, carried away to a far kingdom. All by the hand of God.

*The young and the old lie on the ground in the streets: my virgins and my young men are fallen by the sword; thou hast slain them in the day of thine anger; thou hast killed, and not pitied. Thou hast called as in a solemn day my terrors round about, so that in the day of the Lord's anger none escaped nor remained: those that I have swaddled and brought up hath mine enemy consumed.*

This it will be in the day of the Lord. The same will happen to the nations of the world. Their temples and kings will be cut off. Their strongholds, even the very mountains they flee to, will be struck down. And the streets will be littered with the bodies of the young and old. None will escape the anger of the Lord except those carried away to His kingdom, His servants, on that great and terrible day.

teachings.title: Babylon's fall a picture of the end times
teachings.summary: The prophecy of Babylon's fall carries dual imagery of the final destruction of the spirit of Babylon when Christ avenges the blood of the saints.
teachings.text:
As we near the end of the Book of Jeremiah, we see the prophecy against Babylon, which soon would be crushed by the Medes, establishing the Medo-Persian Empire. Cyrus the Great will eventually restore the remnant of Judah to their land, after the 70 years of captivity, and the 2nd Temple will be built.

But the Lord used Babylon to crush the rebellion of the Jews against Him. To winnow the wheat from the chaff, just as He will the armies of the Beast in the days of vengeance. In this prophecy, we see dual imagery being used; predictions of the soon to come fall of that great Golden empire, but also of the end times. Of the Lord Jesus and the final destruction of that spirit of Babylon, which works even today. And the promise of eternal peace for God's people, the saints who believed on His word. Because God will have justice for the blood of the innocent, the prophets and if the saints that were all slain upon the earth.

teachings.title: The battle of Armageddon
teachings.summary: At Armageddon Christ defeats the beast's armies with the sword of His mouth, casting the antichrist and false prophet into the lake of fire and leaving the wicked to the fowls.
teachings.text:
**Isaiah 13:9**
*Behold, the day of the LORD cometh, cruel both with wrath and fierce anger, to lay the land desolate: and he shall destroy the sinners thereof out of it.*

**Joel 3:12-14**
*Let the heathen be wakened, and come up to the valley of Jehoshaphat: for there will I sit to judge all the heathen round about. Put ye in the sickle, for the harvest is ripe: come, get you down; for the press is full, the fats overflow; for their wickedness is great.*

*Multitudes, multitudes in the valley of decision: for the day of the Lord is near in the valley of decision.*

Armageddon, the "Mountain of Assembly," refers to Mt Zion. The valley of Jehoshaphat, the valley of judgment, is the space between Zion and Mt Olive, where Christ will rule during the Millennial Reign.

It is here the armies of the beast assemble and ride out to battle Jesus,
King Of Kings, And Lord Of Lords.

*And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet that wrought miracles before him, with which he deceived them that had received the mark of the beast, and them that worshipped his image. These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone. And the remnant were slain with the sword of him that sat upon the horse, which sword proceeded out of his mouth: and all the fowls were filled with their flesh.*

The antichrist and his false prophet are instantly cast into the lake of fire. The remnant of their armies slain by the sword that comes from the mouth of Christ. The two-edged sword, which immediately calls to mind the word of God. Spoken from Jesus mouth, with the power to slay the wicked, leaving their carcasses for the carrion birds to feed on.

**Jeremiah 7:33**
*And the carcases of this people shall be meat for the fowls of the heaven, and for the beasts of the earth; and none shall fray them away.*

**Ezekiel 39:17**
*And, thou son of man, thus saith the Lord God; Speak unto every feathered fowl, and to every beast of the field, Assemble yourselves, and come; gather yourselves on every side to my sacrifice that I do sacrifice for you, even a great sacrifice upon the mountains of Israel, that ye may eat flesh, and drink blood.*

teachings.title: The Vials Align with the Trumpets
teachings.summary: The seven vials parallel the seven trumpets in the same wrath period, poured on the damned who harden their hearts rather than repent.
teachings.text:
The 7 vial judgments of the Lord. His wrath and recompense for sin. As all who remain on the earth either worshiped the beast and took the mark, damning themselves or remained unsaved up unto the end of Great Tribulation and the rapture, they and the earth itself suffer the righteous anger and just judgment of the Lord. It is fitting punishment that the saints in Heaven had prayed for, giving glory to the Lord for His wrath has come.

These 7 vials align with the 7 trumpet judgments of chapters 8-11.

Trumpet 1, Vial 1
Trumpet 2, Vial 2
Trumpet 3, Vial 3
Trumpet 4, Vial 4
Trumpet 5, Vial 5
Trumpet 6, Vial 6
Trumpet 7, Vial 7

And are poured out in the same three and a half year period, the second half of Daniel's 70 Weeks. And as we can compare, many of the vials match or enhance the trumpet judgments. There is overlap to the destruction John witnesses and describes.

The first trumpet brings fire to the earth and burns up a third of the trees and all green grass. The vial brings grievous sores upon those with the mark. A judgment of the earth and of man.

The 2nd trump, a mountain burning with fire is cast into the sea, turning a 3rd of the oceans to blood, killing sea life and destroying a third of ships. The 2nd vial, the seas all become blood and all life therein dies. The stink of putrid fish and rancid blood overwhelming the earth.

The third trump and vial; the rivers and fountains of waters, the fresh water of the world, are destroyed. Wormwood making a third of the waters bitter and poisonous, the vial turning the rest to blood that the unrighteous be given blood to drink for they have shed the blood of the saints and prophets and are worthy to have blood to drink.

The fourth trumpet and the fourth vial are poured out upon the sun, and it is given the angels the power to smite the sun and stars and moon that a 3rd of their light is dimmed, and the heat from the sun scorches the wicked who curse God rather than repent and give Him glory in His wrath.

Note that the vast majority this happens to are damned. Twice-dead. They aren't being punished to bring a saving repentance spirituality, admitting they were wrong and that Christ is Lord won't save their souls. But even as these plagues fall upon them, the Bible says, they will remain stiff-necked and hearts hardened. Defiant in their error. Cleaving to their sin. They deserve everything they get.

Darkness comes from both the fifth trumpet and the fifth vial. Abaddon opens the Pitt and the smoke rises up to blot out the dimmed light of the sun. And the beast, the antichrist who still remains on his throne during this period of wrath, sees his kingdom left in darkness. And they that worship the beast blaspheme the name of God for their pains and sores and repent not.

During the sixth trumpet and the sixth vial, you see the great river Euphrates mentioned for both. The river is dried up with the sixth vial and four angels that had been bound beneath the Euphrates are loosed with the sixth trumpet.

As the 7th trumpet sounds and the 7th vial are poured, we see lightnings, voices, thunderings, an earthquake, and great hail. Hail the size of a talent.

The heavy common talent, used in New Testament times, was 58.9 kg (129 lb 14 oz).

Wew.

teachings.title: The Song of Moses and the Song of the Lamb
teachings.summary: The song of Moses is likely Deuteronomy 32, prophesying wrath on Israel for rejecting the Rock, and the song of the Lamb is the new song of Revelation 5.
teachings.text:
*And they sing the song of Moses the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb...*

What are these songs? Many interpret this as one song, but it's clearly stating there are two being sung, one of Moses and the other of the Lamb.

We know that Moses in the Old Testament is credited with two songs. One is sung by Moses and the Israelites upon their successful flight from Egypt giving praise to God for delivering them and warning the nations of the promised land of God's might. This is told in Exodus 15.

The other, in **Deuteronomy 32** which I quoted a couple posts ago, is sung to give everlasting doctrine, that it be sung for all ages by the Israelites to remind them of the Rock of their salvation and prophecy of God's wrath upon them when they eventually forsake God, His law and reject the Messiah, the Christ, who is the Rock. I really suggest going back and reading it again, and consider how clear and prophetic it is regarding precisely what will happen, the apostasy of Israel, the coming of Jesus, and God's destruction of the Jews who don't believe and His wrath on those who reject Jesus.

Most who preach on this subject say the song of Moses is the first song from Exodus, and maybe it is. It's a victory song praising God, but it makes far more sense that the song found in Deuteronomy 32 would be sung just as Jesus' victory is coming, the wrath of God about to be delivered. The judgment of nations which is literally part of the song.

Of course, most who preach on end times Bible prophecy are dispensationalist Zionists who believe the false and wicked doctrine that the end times are a victory for the Jews, rather than Jesus.

The song of the Lamb I believe is the new song mentioned in **Revelation 5**, which we were told was given to the angels and elders to sing, and was entirely about how worthy and great Christ Jesus is to be given this power and glory:

*Saying with a loud voice, Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing.*

Given it is literally a song of the Lamb, it just makes sense this is what John is referring to.

teachings.title: The Winepress of the Wrath of God
teachings.summary: As Abel's blood cried from the ground, the innocent blood of the martyrs brings the grapes of wrath to ripeness.
teachings.text:
But there is another harvest; from the vineyard of the Lord, the grapes of wrath.

*17 And another angel came out of the temple which is in heaven, he also having a sharp sickle.*

*18 And another angel came out from the altar, which had power over fire; and cried with a loud cry to him that had the sharp sickle, saying, Thrust in thy sharp sickle, and gather the clusters of the vine of the earth; for her grapes are fully ripe.*

*19 And the angel thrust in his sickle into the earth, and gathered the vine of the earth, and cast it into the great winepress of the wrath of God.*

*20 And the winepress was trodden without the city, and blood came out of the winepress, even unto the horse bridles, by the space of a thousand and six hundred furlongs.*

Glory, glory, hallelujah.

We know from Cain and Abel in Genesis that the blood of innocents spilled in the earth cries out for God's vengeance. This is a theme repeated in scripture, and the innocent blood of the tribulation and especially that of the martyrs slain in the Great Tribulation, brings the grapes of the vine to fruition. The wrath of God come full. And the winepress is trodden, and the blood that pours out is sufficient to fill a 1,600 furlongs, up to a horse's bridles. A furlong represents a Grecian/Roman measure of a stadia, or 660 feet, thus this measure quoted is 1,000,000 feet. The height of a bridle being 6 feet. That's a lot of blood.

The winepress and the reaping are symbolic of the events like the rapture and the wrath that we see described in more understandable detail elsewhere, but it gives picture to what it actually means and the scope of it all that man's limited mind can comprehend God's awesome work.

teachings.title: Abaddon Is the Destroyer Serving God
teachings.summary: Abaddon is not Satan but the destroying angel of death who serves God, as in the Passover and at Ornan's threshingfloor.
teachings.text:
As the 5th trumpet sounds, we are told of a star, an angel, that falls from the Heavens to earth, who has the key to Hell, and opens the fiery abyss to free the locust-like creatures to torment mankind. He is identified by John in the Hebrew as "*Abaddon,*" in the Greek, "*Apollyon*," which means "Destroyer."

But who is Abaddon?

Many interpreters say this is Satan, fallen to earth and loosening the beasts of Hell to destroy the unbelieving, but the context given in Revelation creates some issues with this, primarily **Revelation 20:1-3**:

*And I saw an angel come down from heaven, having the key of the bottomless pit and a great chain in his hand. And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years, And cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he should deceive the nations no more, till the thousand years should be fulfilled: and after that he must be loosed a little season.*

See the problem? Also, we know that at the Resurrection, Jesus Himself had the keys to Hell and Death. Would He give them over to that old serpent? Seems unlikely.

And, again, we are witnessing God's wrath with the 7 trumpet judgments, these woes poured upon the earth, and so in all things here, these plagues and the angels who are ministering them, are doing so as servants of God.

This is why, in my opinion, Abaddon is the angel of death. An angel of destruction, working in service to God, and not Satan.

And maybe we have seen the "destroyer" doing God's bidding before;

**1 Chronicles 21:15**
*And God sent an angel unto Jerusalem to destroy it: and as he was destroying, the LORD beheld, and he repented him of the evil, and said to the angel that destroyed, It is enough, stay now thine hand. And the angel of the LORD stood by the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite.*

And, perhaps most famously in **Exodus 12:23**:

*For the Lord will pass through to smite the Egyptians; and when he seeth the blood upon the lintel, and on the two side posts, the Lord will pass over the door, and will not suffer the destroyer to come in unto your houses to smite you.*

This is the destroyer. The angel of death. And to him was given the key to Hell, unleashing the nightmarish beasts, with the power to torment men a span of 5 months, was given unto him.

teachings.title: The Army of the Sixth Trumpet Is God's
teachings.summary: As Joel 2 shows, the horsemen of the sixth trumpet are God's army, for Satan is the prince of this world, not the ruler of hell.
teachings.text:
Note the sealed 144,000 are spared the wrath and the woes. And the remaining trees and vegetation, the earth itself is spared. These woes are against man.

And the 6th trumpet sounds and there appears *the four angels which are bound in the great river Euphrates*.

These 4 angels are followed by two hundred million cavalrymen, riding horses with heads of fire-breathing lions and tails like snakes. And they proceed to kill a third of mankind, making war with the armies of man under control of the beast and the false prophet.

Again, many will say that this is the army of Satan, loosed out of Hell, and that the 4 angels bound are devils, fallen and kept in Hell. But there are problems with this.

**Joel 2** contains a prophecy that pictures these end times events, and clearly the army is God's:

*Blow ye the trumpet in Zion, and sound an alarm in my holy mountain: let all the inhabitants of the land tremble: for the day of the Lord cometh, for it is nigh at hand;*

*2 A day of darkness and of gloominess, a day of clouds and of thick darkness, as the morning spread upon the mountains: a great people and a strong; there hath not been ever the like, neither shall be any more after it, even to the years of many generations.*

*3 A fire devoureth before them; and behind them a flame burneth: the land is as the garden of Eden before them, and behind them a desolate wilderness; yea, and nothing shall escape them.*

*4 The appearance of them is as the appearance of horses; and as horsemen, so shall they run.*

*5 Like the noise of chariots on the tops of mountains shall they leap, like the noise of a flame of fire that devoureth the stubble, as a strong people set in battle array.*

*6 Before their face the people shall be much pained: all faces shall gather blackness.*

*7 They shall run like mighty men; they shall climb the wall like men of war; and they shall march every one on his ways, and they shall not break their ranks:*

*8 Neither shall one thrust another; they shall walk every one in his path: and when they fall upon the sword, they shall not be wounded.*

*9 They shall run to and fro in the city; they shall run upon the wall, they shall climb up upon the houses; they shall enter in at the windows like a thief.*

*10 The earth shall quake before them; the heavens shall tremble: the sun and the moon shall be dark, and the stars shall withdraw their shining:*

*11 And the Lord shall utter his voice before his army: for his camp is very great: for he is strong that executeth his word: for the day of the Lord is great and very terrible; and who can abide it?*

In the remaining verses of the chapter, God calls on the people facing His wrath, the unbelieving, those worshipping false gods and idols, to turn towards Him and repent. To be saved and given respite from His terrible wrath.

These angels are servants of God. The army is His. Satan never has control over Hell. He never reigns there in scripture. The Bible says those tormented in Hell do so in the presence of the Lord. Judgment is His.

These may be dark sayings and difficult to hear, and the interpretation of the symbolism and literal events being shown the prophets and John may have multiple meanings, short and long term implications, dual fulfilment, etc...But there can be no doubt that this is entirely of God. Not Satan, whose power is only through the men he may deceive, and the temptations and snares of sin he can convince us of in this world. Not of Heaven, not of Hell.

The Bible says Satan is the prince of this world, not the prince of Hell.

teachings.title: Still They Repented Not
teachings.summary: Even in His wrath God seeks repentance, yet hardened men refuse, and believers should study the timing themselves rather than lean on others.
teachings.text:
The Bible tells us that *The Lord is not slack concerning his promise, as some men count slackness; but is longsuffering to us-ward, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to repentance.*

Even in His wrath and judgment upon the Earth, He seeks repentance of those being afflicted for their wicked hearts. And as we see in Revelation 9, despite the supernatural destruction, the signs and wonders in Heaven, the resurrection of the dead and gathering in the clouds of the elect, the woes and all, the men of the earth will still refuse. Stiff-necked and hearts hardened.

Some folks you just can't reach.

We will see in the following chapter the two witnesses appear in all this, and call the people to repentance preaching in His name. I believe the 144,000 likely are sent to minister the Gospel to those few on Earth who do repent during this time, the three and a half years of wrath before the millennial reign begins.

Of the timing; we know the day of the Lord begins the trumpet judgments. The initial destruction and fire and hail happening quickly. But the 5th trump, the first woe, lasts on earth 5 months (the remaining months of the 4th year, the day of the Lord coming slightly more than 3 and a half years into the Great Tribulation)

Then the armies of God come against man for a year and a month and a day and an hour.

I admit the granular indexing of the exact days and weeks, reflected in Daniels 70 Weeks prophecy from **Daniel 9** can make my eyes glaze over. But people more autistic than I have charted it out and found the days and years matching up with Revelation, and the events foretold. While it is fascinating to consider and a testament to the awesome precision of God's word, I won't get out over my skis trying to explain it. But we can see from these verses there is a timing of things. A way to know when and how long each thing happens.

One of the ways false doctrines evolve surrounding these events is that many are like me, and daunted by some of the more seemingly esoteric aspects, and so they lean heavily on other's interpretation, rather than studying it out themselves.

So make the effort to read and compare scripture with scripture yourself, even if you only get the gist of the timing. Because God reveals it openly. Do not be deceived.

teachings.title: The Trumpets Are Wrath, Not Tribulation
teachings.summary: The trumpet judgments are God's wrath fuelled by the saints' prayers and cannot be confused with the tribulation, and Revelation is meant to reveal.
teachings.text:
God's wrath, the trumpets of war, sounding 7 times (similar to the battle of Jericho where they sounded trumpets 7 times around the city). Only 4 in, and so far there is massive destruction. Unnatural natural disasters. This is the wrath of God fueled by the prayers of the saints. It cannot be confused with the tribulation, even that great tribulation that came just prior to the day of the Lord.

When we get to the second half of the book of Revelation, we will see the 7 vial judgments which, when compared to the 7 trumpet judgments, we will see they are complimentary, in how they affect the earth and its remaining inhabitants, and in their timing. (Chapters 12-22 retell much of 1-11, from a different vantage point, with added details)

It is important to see how things progress, and how the timing is consistent with other scripture that talks about end times Bible prophecy, and just how clear the things stated are. We may see through a glass darkly, but we are given quite a lot of details and signs to watch for, and an order of things that is clear when taken in context. God is not the author of confusion. Revelation means to reveal, not to obscure.

teachings.title: The Plagues of Egypt Picture God's Wrath
teachings.summary: The plagues of Egypt picture the wrath poured out in the trumpets, as prophecy often has dual fulfilment.
teachings.text:
Also, for those unfamiliar with Exodus 5-10 and the 10 plagues that afflicted Egypt due to the harness of Pharaoh's heart, mirror or provide a picture of the judgements poured out on the earth during the days of God's wrath.

The 10 plagues of Egypt in order are: water turning to blood, frogs, lice, flies, livestock pestilence, boils, hail, locusts, darkness, and the killing of firstborn children.

We can already see the water turning to blood, hail and darkness in these first 4 trumps. The exodus of Hebrews from Egypt is a picture of salvation, and a picture of the end times. Most Bible prophecy has dual fulfilment or multiple fulfilments, as the scriptures exist to teach us what was, what is and what shall come.

It's all connected and beautifully so.

teachings.title: The mark on the foreheads
teachings.summary: God's mark on the righteous in Ezekiel 9 is what the beast's mark copies, but God has sealed us with the Spirit unto redemption.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **Ezekiel 9**, the prophet is still being given a vision of Jerusalem, filled with abominations. Some secret, some open and flagrant. Where the people say the Lord had forsaken the earth, or that He seeth not.

And the Lord, come down from the mercy seat, to the threshold of the temple, orders an angel with an inkhorn to set a mark the foreheads of the men who wept and sighed over the abominations in their midst. A righteous remnant.

Those that had charge over the city, the 6 men the Lord summons with their weapons of destruction, I believe angels of the city that kept watch over it. And He orders them to fill the courtyard of the temple with the dead, slaying utterly the old, young, maids and little children that have not the mark.

Of course, Satan has his counterfeit mark;

**Revelation 13:16**
*And he causeth all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond, to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads*

And he orders those that will not worship the beast and his image, and take the mark be killed, making war with the saints. Martyring those who have the testimony of Christ.

This is what the beast is copying. But God has sealed us with the Spirit unto redemption. And those 144K that will come during the wrath will be likewise sealed. God protects His own, while the beast will damn many to torment in the time to come and eternity.

Our Lord will not forsake us. Amen

teachings.title: Antiochus a type of the man of sin
teachings.summary: Antiochus IV pictures the coming Antichrist who will bring false peace, betray the Jews, declare himself God in Jerusalem with a living image, and begin the great tribulation.
teachings.text:
So we see from NT scripture, referencing things past, specifically the type of antichrist epitomized by Antiochus IV Epiphanes, tells us of the future. Of a man of sin, a man of perdition, who will receive power, and who will go *forth conquering, and to conquer.*

He will be given power by other nations. He will bring "peace," with lying and flattery. He will make a treaty with many, and bring in a new word order, a one world government.

He will enter in to Jerusalem, and betray the Jews who likely helped him rise to power, the "days of vengeance."

**Luke 21:20-22**
*And when ye shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh. Then let them which are in Judaea flee to the mountains; and let them which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not them that are in the countries enter thereinto. For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled.*

When the man of sin is seemingly killed by a head wound, he will appear to resurrect, but the beast will be in him, that old serpent. And there, in Jerusalem, he will declare himself God. His prophet, (I believe will be a pope), will confirm this, establishing a one world religion. And everyone will be forced to worship the beast, or die.

There, in the desolation of Jerusalem, he will set up an abomination. Just as Antiochus IV had, a blasphemous idol. But unlike every idol and graven image in scripture that could not move, speak, hear or see, this one will be different:

**Revelation 13:15**
*And he had power to give life unto the image of the beast, that the image of the beast should both speak, and cause that as many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed.*

According to Jesus, this will be when Great Tribulation begins, and His return will be imminent, likely 75 days (Daniel 12:11-12) from the establishment of that image and declaration of godhood by the Antichrist.

teachings.title: Daniel 7 and the Revelation
teachings.summary: Daniel's vision of the beasts parallels Revelation's end-times events, and his fulfilled prophecies show this one is just as sure.
teachings.text:
As we see, the parallels between Daniel's vision and the Revelation of Jesus Christ details the same end times events, with similar imagery. Governments, the beast, his making war on the saints, the Son of Man, the beast having dominion for time, times and half a time, 3.5 years, the destruction of the beast, the saints ruling and reigning with Him, and His judgment against the beast.

This is the start of Daniel's prophetic writing. The parallels will build from here.

What an awesome God we have, Who calls His shots millennia before. The same man, Daniel, who rightly interpreted the coming empires, now is given a glimpse at the end times. We can know God's word is true because the interpretation of the dreams Daniel foretold to the kings all came true. This prophecy of Christ Jesus and the victory over this world is as sure as the prediction of the Greek and Roman empires given a young eunuch in the 6th century BC. Amen

teachings.title: End-times Babylon is not Jerusalem
teachings.summary: Revelation 16 shows Jerusalem divided before Babylon is judged, so they are distinct, and the spirit of Babylon rests on America and the West.
teachings.text:
There is some confusion about what Babylon in Revelation refers to. We see through a glass darkly. But some will claim Jerusalem is end times Babylon based on the similarities between those verses in **Jeremiah 25** and **Revelation 18**.

However we see in **Revelation 16** that this is not the case;

*17 And the seventh angel poured out his vial into the air; and there came a great voice out of the temple of heaven, from the throne, saying, It is done.*

*18 And there were voices, and thunders, and lightnings; and there was a great earthquake, such as was not since men were upon the earth, so mighty an earthquake, and so great.*

*19 And the great city was divided into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell: and great Babylon came in remembrance before God, to give unto her the cup of the wine of the fierceness of his wrath.*

If we note the order of things, that great city, Jerusalem, is divided in thirds by the catastrophic world-wide earthquake that fells all the great cities, and then God turns to Babylon specifically for destruction.

And it is fitting and proper that God bookends His wrath, bringing the utter destruction and desolation against Babylon that they had brought against Jerusalem. Poetic justice as it were.

In my mind, the spirit of Babylon is upon the United States, and the empire that extends across Europe and in other White nations, Canada, Australia, New Zealand. The Idolatry and profane fornication of a people claiming to be of God, yet wicked in every way. Used to destroy other wicked nations by God, and yet still facing His ultimate judgment just as the original Babylon.

teachings.title: The Everlasting Gospel Preached Even in Wrath
teachings.summary: The 144,000 likely minister during the wrath, and the angel with the everlasting gospel shows a God who offers grace to all, not the god of Calvin.
teachings.text:
Here in chapter 14, we are reintroduced to the 144,000 first described in the parallel passage of Revelation 7, and given added details of who they are and whence they came and the seal upon their heads.

These saints, we are told, come from the 12 tribes of Israel, 12,000 from each, who were believers having the testimony of Christ. Virgins, without guile. We know from chapter 7 they will be sent to Earth during the wrath, coming down from Heaven where they are seen here with Jesus. They are sealed, as we are told in chapter 14, with the name of the living God upon their foreheads. These were redeemed among men, the first fruits unto God and the Lamb, who is Christ.

Again, I believe they are sent to minister during the three and a half years of wrath to those who were not saved prior to the rapture. Those that hadn't taken the mark yet during that 75 days that follows the abomination of desolation and the establishment of the antichrist and his false prophet, until the Day of the Lord.

Remember too, that the two witnesses will be preaching during this time. They who were able to stop the rains and call fire down from Heaven.

(It's interesting to note that the antichrist's false prophet is given power to rain fire by Satan, and will be opposed to the witnesses during this time, much like Jannes and Jambres who withstood Moses in the court of Pharaoh, or the prophets )

Even as the grapes of wrath are poured, God would that none perish but come to the saving knowledge of the truth.

John describes seeing an angel flying *in the midst of heaven, having the everlasting gospel to preach unto them that dwell on the earth, and to every nation, and kindred, and tongue, and people, Saying with a loud voice, Fear God, and give glory to him; for the hour of his judgment is come: and worship him that made heaven, and earth, and the sea, and the fountains of waters.*

This is not the god of Calvin. This is not a god selecting those to save and those to condemn. This is a God who so loved the world that even as He rains hail and sends locusts from Hell to torment those who would not repent, who worship the beast, He offers hope through grace to those who can still choose to have faith.

teachings.title: The Beast Promises Peace and Safety
teachings.summary: The beast rises in the beginning of sorrows as a counterfeit Christ promising peace and safety, then blames believers and makes war on the saints.
teachings.text:
**Revelation 13**

*And I stood upon the sand of the sea, and saw a beast rise up out of the sea, having seven heads and ten horns, and upon his horns ten crowns, and upon his heads the name of blasphemy.*

*2 And the beast which I saw was like unto a leopard, and his feet were as the feet of a bear, and his mouth as the mouth of a lion: and the dragon gave him his power, and his seat, and great authority.*

*3 And I saw one of his heads as it were wounded to death; and his deadly wound was healed: and all the world wondered after the beast.*

*4 And they worshipped the dragon which gave power unto the beast: and they worshipped the beast, saying, Who is like unto the beast? who is able to make war with him?*

*5 And there was given unto him a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies; and power was given unto him to continue forty and two months.*

*6 And he opened his mouth in blasphemy against God, to blaspheme his name, and his tabernacle, and them that dwell in heaven.*

To continue: At the beginning of the chapter we are told that there is a beast, the rising antichrist who is given power by Satan. This is the man on the white horse, who was going to conquer, armed with a bow. The son of perdition. He comes to power during the Beginning of Sorrows, the first 4 seals, when there are wars and famines, pestilence and earthquakes, afflicting the whole world.

This tribulation brings the beast to prominence, and the fatal wound that is healed brings him to be worshiped along with Satan who granted him his power.

The world will be in crisis, calling out for a savior and be given a counterfeit Christ who promises the apostate world of non-believers peace and safety.

**Jeremiah 6:14**
*They have healed also the hurt of the daughter of my people slightly, saying, Peace, peace; when there is no peace*.

**1 Thessalonians 5:3**
*For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them, as travail upon a woman with child; and they shall not escape.*

And as he is given power to rule all kingdoms of this earth, a one world government, worshiped as a savior, he begins to make war on the saints.

*7 And it was given unto him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them: and power was given him over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations.*

*8 And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.*

And as the 5th seal opens in **Revelation 6**, the souls of those slain for their testimony of Jesus Christ begin to appear in Heaven.

The beast will blame believers for the tribulations, turning the world against Christians, and this begins the Great Tribulation which is the war against the saints. We see echoes of this even now. As good as called evil and evil good, those who worship Satan and hate God blame us for everything from climate change destroying the planet, to not taking a jab to "stop the spread" of disease, placing the "blood of millions" on our heads. This is a picture of what's to come in the future.

teachings.title: The False Prophet and the Image of the Beast
teachings.summary: The second beast is the false prophet of a one world religion who makes a speaking image of the Antichrist, so believers should flee idolatry now.
teachings.text:
**Revelation 13**
*11 And I beheld another beast coming up out of the earth; and he had two horns like a lamb, and he spake as a dragon.*

*12 And he exerciseth all the power of the first beast before him, and causeth the earth and them which dwell therein to worship the first beast, whose deadly wound was healed.*

*13 And he doeth great wonders, so that he maketh fire come down from heaven on the earth in the sight of men,*

*14 And deceiveth them that dwell on the earth by the means of those miracles which he had power to do in the sight of the beast; saying to them that dwell on the earth, that they should make an image to the beast, which had the wound by a sword, and did live.*

*15 And he had power to give life unto the image of the beast, that the image of the beast should both speak, and cause that as many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed.*

A second beast arises, with the horns of a lamb but the voice of the dragon. This is the false prophet who will be given power by the first beast to make a one world religion that worships the antichrist.

We see in verse 8 that ALL who dwell upon the earth whose names are blotted out of the Book of Life will worship the first beast as a god. Another way of saying this is that those whose names are in the Book of Life, the saved, will not. This is the discernment of the Holy Spirit acting within us. The patience of the saints.

Like Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego who were tempted by Nebuchadnezzar to worship the idol he had decreed all men of Babylon to bow to and refused, willing to be placed in the fiery furnace, so too will the saved by tested.

The second beast, the false prophet who will be the pope of this new world order religion that's formed around its leader as god, will perform what appear to be miracles, calling down fire from heaven.

And he will set up an image of the antichrist to be worshiped. An idol. Beware any religion that allows the worship of idols, now, because they are a picture of this beast religion. Like the jab serving as a picture of the mark, which we are about to discuss, religions of Idolatry are meant to desensitize people over time into accepting this blasphemy. Flee Idolatry.

Not only will the false prophet set up this idol to be worshiped, but he will cause it to move and speak.

**Psalm 115**
*5 They have mouths, but they speak not: eyes have they, but they see not:*

*6 They have ears, but they hear not: noses have they, but they smell not:*

*7 They have hands, but they handle not: feet have they, but they walk not: neither speak they through their throat.*

*8 They that make them are like unto them; so is every one that trusteth in them.*

The Bible tells us again and again how the statues and graven and molten images are as dead and lifeless as the false gods they represent to the idolaters. God mocking idolatry as vanity and superstition. And so here, in the holy place of God as the antichrist sits proclaiming himself as God, an image of him is built to be worshiped by the whole world, and in what will be seen as a miracle, the idol will move and speak as if it were alive.

Many consider this the abomination of desolation as spoken of by Daniel, and given us by Jesus as the sign that the Great Tribulation has begun, to be steadfast as His salvation is at hand.

teachings.title: The Mark of the Beast
teachings.summary: The mark of the beast is how the beast system separates believers for slaughter, but that war is cut short by the sixth seal and the rapture.
teachings.text:
**Revelation 13**
*16 And he causeth all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond, to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads:*

*17 And that no man might buy or sell, save he that had the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of his name.*

*18 Here is wisdom. Let him that hath understanding count the number of the beast: for it is the number of a man; and his number is Six hundred threescore and six.*

The mark of the beast. The culmination of the one world government and religion of Satan. The way the beast system will separate the goats from the sheep for the slaughter.

In modern times, with the technology we have, digital currency and subdermal chips, we can imagine how this system would work.

Understand the context of its implementation too; wars that have devastated the world, great famines, horrible earthquakes and illness on a massive scale.

Billions must die.

And the false savior given power by Satan and fame from his exploits at war and his mock resurrection, the man of perdition, the antichrist comes forth and is declared ruler, a god emperor, and says that believers are the cause of the calamity. That they refuse to go along with the plan of peace and safety. That they even refuse to worship the beast and take his mark, and so they are the enemy.

And for a period described by the Bible in **Daniel 12** as 75 days, the beast will make war on the saints, and overcome them.

But the Bible promises that this time will be cut short by the 6th seal, the Day of the Lord, the rapture of the saints, the dead raised first then those who are alive and remain at the glorious return of Christ.

teachings.title: The Feet of Iron and Clay
teachings.summary: The iron mixed with clay in Daniel 2 is the remnant of Rome that clings to power today, from which the ten kingdoms will give the beast his power.
teachings.text:
Without getting too deep into it, I believe that the 7 empires described in Daniel chapter 2, specifically the feet of mixed iron and miry clay represents where we have been for the past 2000 years. That there is a vestige of the Roman Empire that still clings to power throughout the world, although it's mixed with Myra Clay and isn't fully bonded because of it. And so there are divisions within the kingdoms.

It is from these disparate empires represented by the 10 kingdoms that have an element of Rome still within them, that will end up giving the beast power for the final one world government, the new world order.

The prophecy in Daniel 2 is fascinating. When you consider that the head of gold in the great statute that Nebuchadnezzar dreamed of, represents him and his empire the Babylonians. The following empires, described by Daniel in his interpretation fit perfectly with the empires that followed.

That prophecy held true and is still relevant today thousands of years later. Such is the power of God and his preserved word. Amen

teachings.title: The Woman Is Allegorical Eve
teachings.summary: The woman of Revelation 12 is neither Mary nor modern Israel but best fits an allegorical Eve, closing the Genesis prophecy.
teachings.text:
There are some who say that if chapter 12 is retelling the birth of Christ then, Mary must be who the woman is. But it doesn't fit with the war on the remnant of her seed, or the timing here, thousands of years after her natural death and going to Heaven to wait for the day of redemption, just like every saved believer.

Some say the crown of 12 stars makes the woman Israel, meaning the modern state of those who call themselves Jews. But this is foolish for numerous reasons, especially the repeated verses about those keeping the testimony of Jesus Christ.

As allegorical Eve, we can see a closure with Genesis through her and the prophecy given by God in the Garden. It makes the most sense to me.

As parable it's not literal and interpretation is given us by the Spirit, comparing scripture with scripture. That's the best we can do with some of the symbolism given in these visions. And that's Ok.

teachings.title: The White Horse Rider Is the Antichrist
teachings.summary: The first seal's rider on a white horse is the Antichrist imitating Christ, a man of war seeking one world government, the messiah Talmudic Judaism awaits.
teachings.text:
And so the seven seals of the Great Tribulation are unsealed by the Lord Christ Jesus, and at each a portion of the book is opened to reveal to John what is to come.

And he beheld a white horse, and a man, given a crown and carrying a bow who went forth conquering and to conquer. This is the Antichrist. A leader given power and taking more, riding on a white horse, an imitation of Christ.

The Antichrist, and the many antichrists we are to expect in these, the last days, are not only opposed to the true Christ, but come in His place, using messianic claims and imagery. Here it's given that he will be riding a white horse, symbolic of the coming of Christ, so as to fool everyone who is not saved. His weapon, a bow, showing he is a man of war. His goal will be a one world government, a return to the sin of Babel.

In Talmudic Judaism, especially the eschatology of Chabad Lubavitch, their moshiach or "Messiah" will come as a man who is made a king of war who conquers the world, establishing a throne in Jerusalem. Because they literally worship the Beast of the Antichrist. Satan who gives him power.

The second seal is opened and the red horse of war is loosed upon the earth,

Jesus breaks the third seal, and John sees revealed in the book a black horse; and he that sat on him had a pair of balances in his hand. This is famine. The voice John hears is like a snippet out of time saying "*A measure of wheat for a penny, and three measures of barley for a penny; and see thou hurt not the oil and the wine*."

This is usually interpreted to mean that common commodities, flours of wheat and barley, would be very expensive, a measure, which is a small amount enough to make a single load would cost a penny, which in the Bible usually refers to a days wage for labor. Taking care not to hurt, or spill or waste, the even-more expensive oil and wine.
