The fourth seal is opened, and John is shown a pale horse; *and his name that sat on him was Death, and Hell followed with him.* This is often called pestilence, but it isn't only disease, but all manner of death, flowing from the first 3 horsemen, the Conqueror, the war and the famine. *And power was given unto them over the fourth part of the earth, to kill with sword, and with hunger, and with death, and with the beasts of the earth.*

This is the Great Tribulation preached on by Jesus.

teachings.title: Ezekiel's temple: the offer that will never be
teachings.summary: Ezekiel 40-48 describes a kingdom God graciously offered Israel if they repented, which will now never be because they rejected Christ.
teachings.text:
All this to say that the 5th theory of Ezekiel's Temple is that it is a picture of a promise for an end-times that will now never be. That God was promising the Jews in captivity a chance to make things right. That by His grace and mercy and longsuffering, He was telling them of the glory of the Kingdom of God that He had in mind for them IF they turned back and were faithful.

An alternate ending of things that, though He knew wouldn't come, God was graciously offering Israel, one last time.

And so Jesus came not to judge the world, which He would have had they listened, but to offer salvation.

**John 12:47**
*And if any man hear my words, and believe not, I judge him not: for I came not to judge the world, but to save the world.*

God continued to see His will done, by other means. Because, despite the Calvinist protests, we are given free will, yet our God is not weak and beggarly as Calvin's having to micromanage everything to reach a conclusion He desires. The Lord can let all creation do as all creatures will, and regardless of our choices, still will His Kingdom come.

And so, Ezekiel's Temple will never be. It was an offer that isn't. Not because of a flaw with God, but with the people.

An alternate universe, where **Ezekiel 40-48** serves as **Revelation**. It's the most glaring example of what could have been in the Old Testament end-times prophecy. An achievable promise, rejected by those it was promised to.

teachings.title: Ezekiel's temple points to Christ the true temple
teachings.summary: Ezekiel's temple was the high pattern for a repentant nation to restore God's glory, and Israel's falling short points to Christ who is the true temple.
teachings.text:
The prophecy of Ezekiel's Temple continues, and with much of the measurements and ordinances given, the prophet, and the angelic man with him, witness the return of the glory of God through the east gate, as Ezekiel says, in the like manner he had watched Him depart in the vision of destruction seen in **Ezekiel 9-11**.

*Thou son of man, shew the house to the house of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their iniquities: and let them measure the pattern*.

Here, we are given the purpose of this vision. That this is the pattern of what an ashamed and chastened people would need to restore the glory of God in their midst.

The Lord provides the details of the altar and the sacrifices. The priests and the atonement. The sins of the people are great, putting up pillars to their gods where His temple was, His footstool. The corpses of their kings placed where the sanctified and holy unto God were meant to be. Abominations that caused the desolation and destruction. Restitution and reconciliation offered by ritual cleansing and a resumption of the sacrifices and sin offering.

Another theory regarding Ezekiel's temple is that it is a picture of the Temple in Eternity. That when the last of creation is burned like a scroll, and a New Heaven and New Earth have been given us by God, that this temple would be in place.

Of course, only those justified in Christ Jesus will remain, and our sins will He remember no more.

Our sanctification and redemption will be long past, washed clean in Christ.

So we reject this theory as well.

Given the context of **Ezekiel 43**, we can understand that this is the model of what God would require for a repentant Jewish people, to fully restore the glory among them. The model given them as a nation. Not individual salvation, which is always personal, and by faith in the promises of God, but as a people. A nation. Blessed to have the Lord among them.

The standards were high. Near impossible. But achievable, or God wouldn't have presented it to them. But like the Law, all have fallen short.

**Haggai 2:3**
*Who is left among you that saw this house in her first glory? and how do ye see it now? is it not in your eyes in comparison of it as nothing?*

The temple would never return to this Glory, until the temple of Christ came, was torn down, and on the third day raised up.

**John 2:19-20**
*Jesus answered and said unto them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up. Then said the Jews, Forty and six years was this temple in building, and wilt thou rear it up in three days? But he spake of the temple of his body.*

**Ezekiel 43**’s vision of a glorious temple, when compared to the historical reality of the 2nd Temple, suggests a “falling short” that points to a greater fulfillment. Taken in that point of view, it underscores the need for Jesus Christ, who embodies the true temple, restores God’s presence, and fulfills the prophetic hope of a renewed covenant. And with it a new nation, of every kindred and tongue. The Kingdom of God.

teachings.title: No return to sacrifices in the millennium
teachings.summary: The dispensational claim that temple sacrifices return in a Jewish millennium is another gospel, since salvation was always by faith in Christ's blood.
teachings.text:
Another theory offered for Ezekiel's Temple, is that this would be a temple in the Millennial Kingdom. That the Church is raptured and "not mentioned again after **Revelation 3**."

That the Kingdom is for the Jews.

I would note that Jews aren't mentioned again after chapter 3, and the mentions there aren't good.

But the dispensationalists would have us believe that in the millennium, temple sacrifice returns. That the OT was salvation by works, and we are in the covenant of grace which goes away at the pre-trib rapture.

This is obviously unbiblical and another gospel.

The Jews after the flesh are only promised days of vengeance and being cast out of the Kingdom into outer darkness.

Sacrifices never took away sin. It was always by faith.

*For it is not possible that the blood of bulls and of goats should take away sins.*

Jesus Christ is the lamb slain before the foundation of the world. It was always His blood that believers trusted on, and that faith counted for righteousness.

So we reject that theory as preposterous.

teachings.title: A third temple would not have God's blessing
teachings.summary: Ezekiel's temple cannot be a future third temple built by unbelieving Jews, because God would never accept sacrifices after Christ's finished work or dwell in a house of abominations.
teachings.text:
Yesterday we looked at the theory that the prophecy found in **Ezekiel 40-48** is a picture of a grand design for the 2nd Temple to be built at the end of captivity. A design that the returning Jews failed to achieve, that they fell short of the glory of God. A picture of the shortcomings of the Old Testament, and a picture of why we needed the New.

Another theory regarding Ezekiel's temple is that it describes a future 3rd Temple, a pre-trib, pre-millennial reconstruction undertaken by the Jews in modern Israel, with the help of Zionist dispensationalist Christians, in order to have a place for the Antichrist to defile.

**2 Thessalonians 2:3-4**
*Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition; Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped; so that he as God sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God.*

Now this seems to be a clear prophecy of a 3rd Temple. That there will be a place where sacrifices will be made for the beast to stop, and the abomination of desolation:

**Daniel 9:27**
*And he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease, and for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate, even until the consummation, and that determined shall be poured upon the desolate.*

But a few things are wrong with this theory. As we will see, the presence of God will come into the temple described to Ezekiel. And the sacrifices and the priesthood of Zadok are given in upcoming chapters, as acceptable and commanded of God.

If there is a 3rd Temple, it will not have the blessing of the Father. No sacrifice they make will be pleasing, as they were never what He desired. They were always a picture of Jesus and His sacrifice, which was done once and for all. It is finished. No other sacrifice exists. God would not enter into a house of abominations run by unbelieving Jews. Jews who have no idea who is of Zadok.

There are other theories we will look at, but this one seems to be a stretch.

teachings.title: Ezekiel's temple as the 2nd Temple that fell short
teachings.summary: One theory is that Ezekiel's temple was God's design for the returning exiles' 2nd Temple, which fell short, though it does not fit the site neatly.
teachings.text:
All this math to say, the main theories about what exactly Ezekiel is being shown here, could possibly be correct, but none completely line up with other scripture, history and current topographical reality, in a neat and clear way.

Could this be a command for the 2nd Temple that fell short? Zerubbabel’s temple, smaller in footprint and lacking the expansive courts of Ezekiel’s vision, didn’t match the grand design. This could reflect practical limitations—limited resources, a smaller population, or Persian oversight—falling short of God’s ideal blueprint.

Some Jewish traditions suggest the returned exiles’ efforts were a partial fulfillment, constrained by their circumstances. For all have fallen short of the glory of God.

This theory is especially plausible given the timing of the prophecy. Ezekiel’s temple vision occurs in the 25th year of his exile, around 573 BC, counting from his deportation in 597 BC with King Jehoiachin.

Jeremiah’s prophecy predicts a 70-year exile for Judah, starting with the first Babylonian siege in 605 BC, when Nebuchadnezzar took captives like Daniel. By 573 BC, this marks roughly the 33rd year of Jeremiah’s 70-year timeline. Nearly the halfway point of the captivity.

Also, the description of the sacrifices and the continued elevation of the Levitical line of the sons of Zadok (rather than Aaron, a change made by Solomon in **1 Kings 2**) as the high priests, marks it as of the time of the 2nd Temple.

It would be counter to the New Testament that we are under to have a priestly caste and animal sacrifices in a temple that, as we will see, has the presence of God within.

But again, the problem is that if this was the expectation of God's perfect plan that the Jews returning from captivity failed to achieve, it wouldn't fit on the very site that was given. Assuming cubits are consistent.

There are other theories we can explore as this continues. But again, we see through a glass darkly and we should be open to the idea that some things we just don't know.

teachings.title: The New Testament clarifies Ezekiel's prophecy
teachings.summary: Older non-dispensational commentators let Revelation separate the pre- and post-millennial battles that Ezekiel saw darkly, and it is fine not to know every detail.
teachings.text:
Getting commentary support for the Fundamentalist view that the New Testament clarifies prophecy that the Old Testament saw through a glass darkly, is difficult because most commentaries and writing on **Ezekiel 38-39** is dispensational. And they all see it through the lens of modern Israel and Zionism.

Matthew Henry (1662–1714), A non-dispensational premillennialist, views **Ezekiel 38–39** as a unified prophecy of a future attack on God’s people, defeated by divine intervention. But he saw the New Testament, particularly Revelation, as clarifying its eschatological significance. He connects **Ezekiel 39:17–20** (birds’ feast) to **Revelation 19:17–21** (pre-millennial battle) and **Ezekiel 38**’s Gog-Magog to **Revelation 20:7–10** (post-millennial rebellion), but treats Ezekiel 38–39 as a single prophecy.

James Burton Coffman (1905–2006), a premillennialist with non-dispensational leanings, Coffman interprets **Ezekiel 38–39** as a single “world-judgment” prophecy, with Revelation providing clarity. He aligns **Ezekiel 39:17–20** with **Revelation 19:17–18** (pre-millennial battle) and notes **Ezekiel 38**’s Gog-Magog terminology resembles **Revelation 20:7–10** (post-millennial rebellion). While not explicitly arguing for two events or a reversed order, he suggests Ezekiel's prophecy conflates imagery that **Revelation** properly separates into pre- and post-millennial battles.

What we should take away from this is it is ok to not know, and trust God's word.

teachings.title: Don't break fellowship over prophecy timing
teachings.summary: After weighing the theories on Ezekiel 38-39 and Revelation 20, he teaches that holding hard positions on prophetic timing is foolish when the saved will all witness it.
teachings.text:
The dispensationalist view is that the OT prophecy is entirely about Tribulation, where Revelation 20 is an entirely different battle. But this is Jew-focused understanding, to say Gog and Magog will invade Israel before the wrath, that it is current and geopolitical, and imminent.

Then, there's another opinion, that Gog and Magog of **Ezekiel 38-39** is entirely the same as the post-millenial battle of **Revelation 20**, with added details.

The 7 years of burying bodies and burning weapons happens between the defeat of their armies and the casting of Satan into the lake of fire, and the Great White Throne judgment. Between **Revelation 20:1**0 and **1**1. That Revelation is the highlights, and **Ezekiel 39** gives more details.

We know the millennium applies to Satan's captivity bound in Hell, not the entire period that the Kingdom exists on Earth.

We don't know the length of the little season. We don't know the amount of time that passes to build the armies and gather weapons in that multitude. We don't have any indication (no " immediately after") to tell us that following the battle of **Revelation 20**, Gog and Magog, how much time elapses before the judgment of the Dead.

This theory postulates that **Ezekiel 37** is the resurrection, **Ezekiel 38** is the millennial reign into the battle of Gog and Magog, and **Ezekiel 39** just provides additional details of the aftermath of the battle.

Maybe!

This is why it is so foolish to hold a hard and fast opinion about end times Bible prophecy that leads you to break fellowship with other gospel professing Christians.

The good news is that if you have trusted on the blood of Christ and accepted that free gift of Salvation, we will be there to witness it. And in the end that's more important than arguing over the timing of things then, today.

teachings.title: Gog and Magog are the armies of the world
teachings.summary: Ezekiel 38 describes the same post-millennial attack as Revelation 20, when Satan deceives the nations against the camp of the saints, not one or two modern nations.
teachings.text:
Here in **Ezekiel 38**, the prophet is given the vision of Gog, and Magog which is reflected in John's Revelation of Jesus Christ, chapter 20. They both are the same prophecy, describing the same future event.

A lot of people get confused about Gog and Magog. There is a lot of eschatology and charts and predictions about who these are and what it means in current times.

God is not the author of confusion.

In the previous chapter Ezekiel prophesied about the coming millennial Kingdom. The resurrection of them dry bones and a restoration of Zion, and that beloved city, under the reign of Christ, the Son of David. Jesus ruling and reigning.

Note the setting, after many days, in the later years. The mountains of Israel that had been waste, is dwelling safely those brought forth from many nations, God's people of Israel.

And these nations will have an evil thought, and seek to spoil the camp of the saints. Cities without walls. The redeemed of God living peacefully. Satan deceiving the heathen to go against Jesus and His saints. To spoil us.

This will be a day of wrath and the armies of innumerable people will be destroyed by fire and other supernatural means. And the Lord will be sanctified by these events.

There is no dual fulfilment here. This is a future event that has no happened. The nations of Japheth and Ham mentioned fall on both sides. It's not ethnic, there's people of all nations in Jerusalem and in the armies of Gog.

We don't know what the maps will look like in the millennial Kingdom. We don't know how that will shake out, over the 1,000 years of Christ ruling with a rod of iron, and we who are saved His priests.

It isn't difficult to understand as long as you're willing to accept this is a literal future event. And Gog and Magog are armies of the world, not one or two nations that fit some current geopolitical theories.

teachings.title: Gog and Magog mapped onto every generation's enemies
teachings.summary: For decades Christians identified Gog and Magog with whatever nation was their current enemy, ignoring the scriptural timing that puts it after the millennium.
teachings.text:
During the 1940s to 1990s, various theories emerged about the identities of Gog and Magog, often reflecting the geopolitical climate of the time.

In the 1940s, some Christians associated Gog and Magog with Nazi Germany and Imperial Japan, tying them to their roles as aggressors in World War II.

From the 1950s through the 1980s, it became popular in evangelical circles to identify Gog as the Soviet Union and Magog as its satellite states or China, driven by Cold War fears of communism.

In the 1980s, Ronald Reagan and New Christian Right leaders specifically linked Gog to the Soviet Union, emphasizing its communistic and atheistic nature.

 Following the Soviet Union's collapse in the 1990s, some speculated Gog and Magog could represent Russia and allies like Iran, influenced by Middle Eastern conflicts.

By the late 1990s, George W. Bush connected Gog to Iraq, citing biblical prophecy especially post-9/11.

These interpretations consistently mapped biblical figures onto contemporary geopolitical rivals, ignoring the timing given in scripture.

They would conflate the battle of Armageddon that comes at the return of Christ on the day of the Lord, at the beginning of wrath and before the Millennium, with the events described here, which occurs afterwards.

Handy to blame your current enemies as the enemies of God. But it isn't cut and dry and it is not possible to prove who makes up the final army of Satan when we're are always more than 1,000 years away from it happening.

teachings.title: Ezekiel's temple as what could have been
teachings.theme: The new heavens and new earth
teachings.summary: Ezekiel's temple may be read as what could have been, since God with foreknowledge set conditional promises before Israel under the Mosaic covenant, which they failed to keep.
teachings.text:
Here in **Ezekiel 45**, the instructions for a temple and a time where there will be a priesthood of Zadok, Levites given land by cast lots for suburbs around the restored Temple. And sacrifices made for various offerings, the measure of which are given for "just balances," precise volumes, that nothing is cheated or anyone give more than another.

Similar to the existing Levitical laws, given unto Moses, the prophesied Temple in **Ezekiel 40-48** has similar Old Testament offerings and carnal ordinances, Sabbaths and holy days, done away with in the reformation of the New Testament.

We have looked at 4 main theories regarding this prophecy.; that it is symbolic and represents the church in Christ and Jesus our temple.

That it is literal, meant to be the design for the 2nd Temple Ezra will begin after captivity. That they fell short in grandeur and size.

That it is a future Temple, for the 3rd Temple leading up to the beginning of the Tribulation.

That it is a Temple in the millennial Kingdom, or in the eternal Kingdom.

All these theories have problems that make them more and more unlikely to be true. The secret things are His and we see through a glass darkly, but surely there's a purpose and a reason for Ezekiel to cap off his end times prophecies, that extend back to chapter 33. That the restoration promised also applies to the prophecy of the Temple.

Which brings us to another theory which I truthfully hadn't considered before. The interpretation of "what could have been."

First, we must acknowledge that God knows the end from the beginning, and the invisible things of what hasn't happened yet.

**Isaiah 46:9-10**
*Remember the former things of old: for I am God, and there is none else; I am God, and there is none like me, Declaring the end from the beginning, and from ancient times the things that are not yet done, saying, My counsel shall stand, and I will do all my pleasure.*

God knows our decisions before we make them, but also allows us the free will to make them, and gives constant appeals to repentance, and encourages us to choose His ways and seek His paths.

The Lord gave the covenant to Israel through Moses with this clear understanding.

**Deuteronomy 30:15-20**
*See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil; In that I command thee this day to love the Lord thy God, to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply: and the Lord thy God shall bless thee in the land whither thou goest to possess it. But if thine heart turn away, so that thou wilt not hear, but shalt be drawn away, and worship other gods, and serve them; I denounce unto you this day, that ye shall surely perish, and that ye shall not prolong your days upon the land, whither thou passest over Jordan to go to possess it. I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live: That thou mayest love the Lord thy God, and that thou mayest obey his voice, and that thou mayest cleave unto him: for he is thy life, and the length of thy days: that thou mayest dwell in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob, to give them.*

God made these conditional promises to Israel as a nation, with the foreknowledge that they would fail. Unlike the Abrahamic and Davidic covenants, which were mostly unconditional (depending on the men themselves to believe God, and have it counted for righteousness), the Mosaic covenant, with the commandments and Levitical laws, depended on the people to keep up their end in order to obtain the Kingdom and the promises and the blessings that would come if they would. And in His grace, multiple opportunities for restitution if they failed.

**2 Chronicles 7:14**
*If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.*

teachings.title: Ezekiel's temple: a promise on condition
teachings.theme: The new heavens and new earth
teachings.summary: The temple vision was a conditional promise to Israel of Christ and a kingdom if they repented, which they refused, as Christ lamented over Jerusalem.
teachings.text:
Ezekiel is no different. It is the explicit purpose of the Temple prophecy, giving the people a promise, contingent on their getting right:

**Ezekiel 43:10-11** 
*Thou son of man, shew the house to the house of Israel, that they may be ashamed of their iniquities: and let them measure the pattern. And if they be ashamed of all that they have done, shew them the form of the house, and the fashion thereof, and the goings out thereof, and the comings in thereof, and all the forms thereof, and all the ordinances thereof, and all the forms thereof, and all the laws thereof: and write it in their sight, that they may keep the whole form thereof, and all the ordinances thereof, and do them*.

The promises given the people included Christ, and a Kingdom, if they repented towards the Law and God.

**Zachariah 6:12-15**
*Thus speaketh the Lord of hosts, saying, Behold the man whose name is* The Branch*; and he shall grow up out of his place, and he shall build the temple of the Lord: Even he shall build the temple of the Lord; and he shall bear the glory, and shall sit and rule upon his throne; and he shall be a priest upon his throne: and the counsel of peace shall be between them both. And the crowns shall be to Helem, and to Tobijah, and to Jedaiah, and to Hen the son of Zephaniah, for a memorial in the temple of the Lord. And they that are far off shall come and build in the temple of the Lord, and ye shall know that the Lord of hosts hath sent me unto you. And this shall come to pass, if ye will diligently obey the voice of the Lord your God.*

They could be children of the Kingdom if they were ashamed of their abominations, took the chastening God consistently gave them, and like the heathen of Nineveh, turned from the wicked ways,

God sent prophets, and they killed them. God wiped out the Northern Kingdom as an example. He brings Judah into bondage under Babylon, and makes His holy city desolate. All to goad them to come to repentance that they would be His people, and He would be their God.

**Matthew 23:37**
*O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!*

teachings.title: No temple in the eternal state
teachings.theme: The new heavens and new earth
teachings.summary: Ezekiel's temple cannot be in eternity because Revelation 21 says the Lord God and the Lamb are the temple of New Jerusalem.
teachings.text:
To further refute the Temple of Eternity theory;

**Revelation 21:22-23**
*And I saw no temple therein: for the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple of it. And the city had no need of the sun, neither of the moon, to shine in it: for the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof.*

The heavenly Jerusalem has no temple, because the Lord God Almighty and the Lamb are the temple. Ezekiel describes a very physical building, with very specific dimensions and chambers and purposes. The doors and windows. The altar.

None of this exists or is needed in the eternal state, because the Lord is with us. No need for the Sun or light, because His glory *is* our light.

His glory will not depart. His glory will not therefore return, because He will be ever present with us. Sacrifice will not be needed, as our sins are remembered no more. Amen

teachings.title: To Him did all prophets give witness
teachings.theme: The new heavens and new earth
teachings.summary: Isaiah 66, quoted throughout the New Testament, encapsulates the believer's hope of a new heaven and earth, Christ's judgment of the wicked, and rest for those who trust Him.
teachings.text:
I'm running late and I will come back to this but in the meantime here are a list of New Testament verses that directly quote or allude to **Isaiah 66**:

**Acts 7:49-50**

**Matthew 5:34-35**

**2 Thessalonians 1:7-8**

**Revelation 19:11-15**

**2 Peter 3:13**

**Revelation 21:1**

**Mark 9:42-48**

A new Heaven and a new Earth, Jesus having the Earth as His footstool. Slaying with the sword that proceedeth out of His mouth. And fiery flame of judgment. And those who trust in Him entering into His rest.

The final chapter of Isaiah, like the final book of the Bible, the Revelation of Jesus, perfectly encapsulates the hope that we have set before us.

To Him did all prophets give witness.

teachings.title: The new Jerusalem in Jeremiah 31
teachings.theme: The new heavens and new earth
teachings.summary: Jeremiah 31 has a dual fulfilment: the return from Babylon and the new Jerusalem in Christ for scattered believers of all nations.
teachings.text:
**Jeremiah 31** picks up immediately after chapter 30; *The fierce anger of the Lord shall not return, until he hath done it, and until he have performed the intents of his heart: in the latter days ye shall consider it.* With God promising His people that their captivity is temporary, a refining process to bring them back to repentance and punish the wicked.

No longer will the iniquity of men be felt by their children. No more men eating sour grapes and their children's teeth being set on edge. We will each stand in Christ or fall to our own sin in a final judgment.

But more, as He does in chapter 31, God gives Jeremiah a prophecy that not only applies to the people in Babylon who will be restored at the end of the 70yrs, but a larger promise to all Israel, and a restoration of a new Jerusalem that encompasses the entire region. That promise, as we see in Hebrews, is in Christ and it is offered to all the scattered believers in all nations, from every shore. And it is a new Jerusalem.

**Revelation 21:16**
 *And the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth: and he measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal.*

The dual fulfilment of prophecy provides us with a window into the judgment of God and an understanding of His promises and His delivering on them. To give us reason to trust the word of God. And we are blessed to have the revelation of the New Testament to understand what was unclear in the Old. That we who walk in His word may be comforted by faith in His promise and the knowledge of the kingdom to come, in Christ Jesus.

teachings.title: The thousand years Satan is bound
teachings.theme: The new heavens and new earth
teachings.summary: Post-millennialism and amillennialism err because the thousand years is the time Satan is bound after the wrath and Armageddon, which is clearly not now or past.
teachings.text:
Post-millennialism and amillennialism are as unbiblical as pre-trib rapture and dispensationalist Zionism.

The mistake those who adopt the position that either the millennium of Revelation is figurative or worse, currently happening, is that they mistakenly believe the 1000 years refers to Christ's reign, rather than the period of time Satan is bound while Christ rules and reigns with the saints, following the wrath of God being poured out and the battle of Armageddon.

This misunderstanding leads to error. Clearly this millennium isn't now, as Satan is clearly not bound, and is free to deceive men and nations. It's not past, because since Christ there has been no period where Satan wasn't on earth like a *roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour.*

The "it's not literal"/The kingdom means in Heaven/amillennialist approach doesn't account for Satan being loosed at the end of the 1000 years, the battle of Gog and Magog that follows, the total destruction of Heaven and Earth, Hell being thrown into the Lake of Fire, New Heaven and New Earth, etc, or how any of that makes sense if we are all in Heaven and Christ isn't ruling on old, current earth.

teachings.title: Make haste, my beloved: praying for His return
teachings.summary: The Song ends in prayer for the beloved to come quickly, the believer's prayer of Maranatha for the day of the Lord, the gathering of His people and His wrath on the ungodly.
teachings.text:
The Song of Solomon ends with prayer. She calls upon the Lord, acknowledging that the companions of God hear His voice. His sheep. She asks, humbly, to hear His voice as He calls.

We should always listen for that still, small voice. We should pray that God gives us ears to hear His will.

Her final prayer is that her love come quickly. To make haste in His return, to come down upon the mountains, as a roe or young hart, gazelle among the spices.

The prayer for *Thy Kingdom, come.* Or *Even so, come, Lord Jesus,* is found throughout scripture. *Maranatha,* come quickly.

**2 Peter 3:12**
*Looking for and hastening unto the coming of the day of God, wherein the heavens being on fire shall be dissolved, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat?*

This is our hope, for the day of the Lord. His gathering of His people, the resurrection of the saints into glory. His terrible and fearful wrath on the ungodly.

As mature Christians, we should be as the woman, gladly giving ourselves to the Lord, and praying to hear His voice, praying for His return. She has come to understand love, through Him. And has gladly given herself to Him.

teachings.title: The days are at hand
teachings.summary: Like the proverb Ezekiel rebuked, last-days scoffers say His coming is delayed, but His word will come to pass.
teachings.text:
And again, the word of God came to him, and says there is a proverb in the land that offends the Lord. That their days are prolonged and every vision faileth. That things are fine, and the prophecy of God is not coming true.

Much like the scoffers we have in these last days;

**2 Peter 3:3-4**
*Knowing this first, that there shall come in the last days scoffers, walking after their own lusts, And saying, Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation.*

The Lord God hates scoffers, and says to Ezekiel that He will make this proverb to cease. The day is at hand, not prolonged. And the effect of every vision will be made true.

*For I am the Lord: I will speak, and the word that I shall speak shall come to pass; it shall be no more prolonged: for in your days, O rebellious house, will I say the word, and will perform it, saith the Lord God.*

Fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, and their lack of fear or respect has angered Him. Imagine the fury of the Lord today.

But the days are short and will not be prolonged, but the word which He has spoken shall be done. Even so, hurry Lord. Amen

teachings.title: Peace and safety, then sudden destruction
teachings.summary: False prophets cry peace, but watchful believers know the signs and seasons, while the day of the Lord comes as a thief only on the unready.
teachings.text:
**1 Thessalonians 5:1-3**
*But of the times and the seasons, brethren, ye have no need that I write unto you. For yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night. For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them, as travail upon a woman with child; and they shall not escape.*

Jeremiah continues his fire breathing preaching against the people of Judah. And in chapter 8, God's judgment again singles out the false prophets and in this passage, the scribes, for being worthless to the people.

The prophets claiming there is peace in the land and with God. That the abominations the people have committed aren't coming to a head. That the wrath of God wasn't coming.

The scribes, transcribing copies of the law, by the letter and not the spirit, that the people should repent towards God.

God uses the timing of things found in nature, the crane and the storm in their daily migration at dawn and dusk. As the harvest comes in fall when the summer is over.

These signs are ours to see as well. And we who are sober and watchful are given these signs that we may know tribulation is coming for a people.

**Matthew 24:32-33**
*Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh: So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.*

The times and seasons are observable to us, but to the backslidden and to the unregenerate, the day of the Lord comes as a thief in the night.

But we know the signs, as Christ told us;

*Take heed that no man deceive you. For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many. And ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars: see that ye be not troubled: for all these things must come to pass, but the end is not yet. For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be famines, and pestilences, and earthquakes, in divers places.All these are the beginning of sorrows.*

The judgment of nations or the final day of the Lord, the signs and the seasons are known to us, if we remain vigilant and blamelessly walking in the Spirit, ready to be delivered.

teachings.title: Take heed: the end is not yet
teachings.summary: In the Olivet discourse Jesus warns that false Christs, wars, disasters and persecution are only the beginning of sorrows and not the sign of His return.
teachings.text:
End times Bible prophecy. The one area of study where we continue to see through a glass darkly. But, for the elects' sake, those of us chosen in Christ, who diligently keep watch, we have been given the knowledge of the signs of the season that we not be caught unawares. That Jesus doesn't come as a thief in the night to those with eyes to see.

And so, here in Mark's version of the Olivet discourse, where Jesus teaches some of the apostles, and by way of the Holy Spirit, teaches ourselves, what will be and what to look for, that we may be ready and be saved, should the great tribulation come in our day.

First, in response to a disciple wondering at the great temple, Jesus says not a stone on top of another will remain standing. This prophecy was fulfilled in 70AD.

Some mistake this as meaning all that follows was fulfilled at that time, which is not supported. Jesus tells us of future events, far outlasting the 1st century, and signs that we have yet to see.

Biblical teaching is that we have been in the "end times" from the moment of Jesus ascension on Pentecost. These are the last days. And until the abomination of desolation is revealed and the sun and moon darkens, that like the fig tree budding signals summer, and Christ returns in His glory in the clouds, as angels gather we elect to join Him, we shall remain in these, the last days.

And so Jesus begins by warning "*Take heed lest any man deceive you*." There will be false Christs who, if it were possible would deceive even believers. This we have seen throughout history, and witness it today. Many would be Messiahs, especially of the Jew, rising in prominence and power. False prophets and accused fake churches, claiming to be of Christ. Jesus and the apostles warn of this for good reason. *Even now there are many antichrists.* And thus shall it be till the end. *For many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and shall deceive many.*

*And when ye shall hear of wars and rumours of wars, be ye not troubled: for such things must needs be; but the end shall not be yet. For nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: and there shall be earthquakes in divers places, and there shall be famines and troubles: these are the beginnings of sorrows.*

Jesus is still giving warning to not be deceived as to when the end comes. He says we will hear of wars and rumors of wars. Great kingdoms clashing. But we aren't to be troubled, because that's not the sign of His coming. These things are always happening. Same with earthquakes and famines and other tribulations, both man made and naturally occurring, that the superstitious and the fearful seize on to say "this is it! It must be the end of the world!"

Be not troubled, the end is not yet. This is just the beginning of sorrows. These are things that simply are. That must be.

So, he's warned us that we should watch for false Christ's and not be troubled or seek as a sign things like wars and disasters. What the natural man would see as a sign.

And further, as a warning to His disciples, says they are going to be brought before rulers and the Jews of the synagogue of Satan to be persecuted and murdered for His name's sake. And that the Gospel must first be published in every nation. He is still warning them that they not be afraid. That they not take their persecution as the sign that the end is here, and understand that it is a testimony against the rulers of this world and how the Gospel is spread to every creature. He is encouraging them, and us as Christians to understand that this is still the case throughout the last days. First century AD, right up until the end.

Remember the apostles there asked for the signs to know when the day of redemption would be, and so Jesus is laying the groundwork for what NOT to take as a sign that His return was imminent. False Christs, wars and calamity, disasters and famines, the persecution of the saints in the publishing of the Gospel to all nations.

He's saying these things will all happen for sure, but be not troubled, it isn't the end.

teachings.title: This generation shall not pass
teachings.summary: This generation means those alive when the signs come to pass, and dispensationalists twist the verse to obscure the plain meaning of the Olivet discourse.
teachings.text:
And so this is the parable of the fig tree. This is the sign that it's soon. *So likewise ye, when ye see these things come to pass, know ye that the kingdom of God is nigh at hand.*

*Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass away, till all be fulfilled.*

This last verse confuses many. They ignore that this generation refers to the people alive and present when these things come to pass, and instead say that Jesus was speaking directly to the apostles in front of Him and their generation.

It's this confusion and other deliberate distortions of these scriptures that dispensationalists seize on to change the plain meaning of the Olivet discourse regarding the end times. They make it more complicated than it is, and trust those they are misleading won't understand the scripture. Exactly what Christ gave warning to beware.

teachings.title: Watch ye therefore
teachings.summary: Since no man knows the day or hour, believers must watch, stay sober and be faithful stewards so the Lord finds them ready.
teachings.text:
And so, knowing all this, and understanding what to look out for and what to be wary against, what shall we do? Christ tells us.

*But of that day and that hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels which are in heaven, neither the Son, but the Father. Take ye heed, watch and pray: for ye know not when the time is.*

*For the Son of Man is as a man taking a far journey, who left his house, and gave authority to his servants, and to every man his work, and commanded the porter to watch. Watch ye therefore: for ye know not when the master of the house cometh, at even, or at midnight, or at the cockcrowing, or in the morning; Lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping. And what I say unto you I say unto all, Watch.*

Watch. Be prepared. Be sober and vigilant. Not carried away by the cares of this world. Not in fear of the tribulation of this world. Not fooled by false prophets.

We are to watch and be good stewards who sow increase for the Lord. Be like the virgins prepared for the bridegroom, who filled their lamps with oil. Be like a servant left with 10 talents of silver, who increased his master's treasure.

Watch and be ready, that on that great day Jesus greats you saying "well done my trusty servants. Well done."

**Matthew 24:24**

You notice it doesn't say only certain Christians. People who aren't backsliding. Doesn't say people who go to church three times a week and read their Bible everyday. It says the elect. So that's every saved Christian.

teachings.summary: Says taking the mark of the beast requires worshipping the beast and his image, and that Revelation 22:18-19 warns those who add to or take from scripture.
teachings.text:
Taking the Mark of The Beast requires one to worship the beast and his image.

*For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect...And he causeth all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond, to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads...And the beast was taken, and with him the false prophet that wrought miracles before him, with which he deceived them that had received the mark of the beast, and them that worshipped his image. These both were cast alive into a lake of fire burning with brimstone....And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them: and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God, and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.*

No one who is saved will worship the beast to take his mark. No person who takes the mark will repent and be saved, they are blotted out of the book of life, the Bible says. Reprobates. Rejected of God.

Beware false prophets who seek to tell you that there is no such thing as being given up for holding the truth in unrighteousness. Who say you can be forgiven for blasphemy of the holy Spirit, when Jesus says there is no forgiveness for it. That there aren't reprobates, when the Jews who hardened their hearts were damned, unable to hear the truth and be healed.

Finally, **Revelation 22:18-19** is clear; anyone who adds to scripture or takes away from scripture is blotted out of the book of life, and accursed.

*For I testify unto every man that heareth the words of the prophecy of this book, If any man shall add unto these things, God shall add unto him the plagues that are written in this book: And if any man shall take away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God shall take away his part out of the book of life, and out of the holy city, and from the things which are written in this book.*

Jesus Christ Himself testifies that this is true. His last command in the final chapter of the final book of the Bible.

No one is ever written into the book of life once they've been removed.

teachings.title: Neither... nor in Daniel 11:37
teachings.summary: Walks through the grammar of 'neither... nor' to show that Daniel 11:37 says the antichrist will regard neither the God of his fathers, nor the desire of women, nor any god.
teachings.text:
***Neither shall he regard** the God of his fathers, nor the desire of women...*

For the non-English speaker, understanding basic grammar can be a stumbling block for understanding God's word.

"Neither... nor" is a negative correlative conjunction that connects two or more parts of a sentence to indicate that both options are not true.

"Neither... nor" must be used in parallel structures, meaning both sides must be balanced. For example, if "neither" is followed by a verb, "nor" must also be followed by a verb, or call back to the original verb, and apply it equally to the object of the sentence. For example;

"Neither shall he regard":

"Shall" is the main verb, with "he" as the subject. "Neither" is a coordinating conjunction modifying the verb "shall regard."

"The God of his fathers" is the direct object of "regard."
("The" modifies "God." "Of his fathers" is a prepositional phrase modifying "God.")

"Nor" introduces the second object, "desire" which parallels "God."

("The" modifies "desire."
"Of women" is a prepositional phrase modifying "desire.")

So in the verse about the antichrist, taken from **Daniel 11:37**

*Neither shall he regard the God of his fathers, nor the desire of women, nor regard any god: for he shall magnify himself above all.*

...the Bible says that the antichrist shall not regard the God of his fathers, shall not regard the desire of women, nor shall he regard any god, (small L lords.) Why? For (because, for this reason) he shall magnify himself above all.

It's easy to get caught in strange doctrine and weird beliefs when you don't understand how our language works. Especially when you refuse to attend church and despise correction.

teachings.title: The Olivet Discourse was spoken to believers
teachings.summary: Shows from the use of ye and they that Jesus spoke the Olivet Discourse to His disciples, with redemption drawing nigh for them.
teachings.text:
**Isaiah 7:14 **
*Therefore the Lord himself shall give you a sign; Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.*

**Isaiah 9:6 **
*For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder: and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace*.

**Micah 5:2 **
*But thou, Bethlehem Ephratah, though thou be little among the thousands of Judah, yet out of thee shall he come forth unto me that is to be ruler in Israel; whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting.*

To Him gave all the prophets witness.
Amen

Dispensationalists falsely claim that the Olivet Discourse found in **Matthew 24, Luke 21** and **Mark 13** are "written to the Jews, not believers. There is no evidence of this, but there is clear evidence that Jesus was speaking to His disciples, believers, and made a clear distinction between "ye" and "they."

**Luke 21:7-28**
*And they asked him, saying, Master, but when shall these things be? and what sign will there be when these things shall come to pass? And he said, Take heed that **ye** be not deceived: for many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and the time draweth near: go **ye** not therefore after them. But when **ye** shall hear of wars and commotions, be not terrified: for these things must first come to pass; but the end is not by and by. Then said he unto them, Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom: And great earthquakes shall be in divers places, and famines, and pestilences; and fearful sights and great signs shall there be from heaven. But before all these, they shall lay their hands on **you**, and persecute **you**, delivering you up to the synagogues, and into prisons, being brought before kings and rulers for my name's sake. And it shall turn to **you** for a testimony. Settle it therefore in your hearts, not to meditate before what **ye** shall answer: For I will give you a mouth and wisdom, which all **your** adversaries shall not be able to gainsay nor resist. And **ye** shall be betrayed both by parents, and brethren, and kinsfolks, and friends; and some of **you** shall they cause to be put to death. And **ye** shall be hated of all men for my name's sake. But there shall not an hair of **your** head perish. In your patience *possess ye your* souls. And when **ye** shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.

Then let **them** which are in Judaea flee to the mountains; and let **them** which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not **them** that are in the countries enter thereinto. **For these be the days of vengeance**, that all things which are written may be fulfilled. But woe unto **them** that are with child, and to **them** that give suck, in those days! for there shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon **this people**. And **they** shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.

And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity; the sea and the waves roaring; Men's hearts failing **them** for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken. And then shall **they** see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory. And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and **lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.***

Jesus speaking to saved Christians, His disciples, uses "ye" and "you," but talking about the unbelieving Jews, uses "they" and "this people."

"They" get the days of vengeance. "Ye" get "your redemption." It's a clear distinction. It is not "written to the Jews," but to believers.

teachings.title: The order of events: tribulation, then the gathering
teachings.summary: Says Jesus gave the order of events, with the rapture after the tribulation and before the wrath of God, matching Revelation 6, 7, 13 and 14.
teachings.text:
Pre-tribbers hate this. But Jesus was very clear, this is the order of events.

This is the same order of events given in Revelation 6 and 7.

There is no secret rapture before the tribulation. There is a very public and unquestionable rapture before the wrath of God is poured out, after the tribulation.

Revelation 13 and 14 give the same events from a different perspective. The beast makes war upon the saints. This is the great tribulation. And the harvest is the rapture.

teachings.title: The Olivet Discourse and the destruction of the temple
teachings.summary: Reads Luke 21 on the destruction of the second temple and the signs of the end, noting that believers need not fear and Christ's return will be open and visible, not secret.
teachings.text:
**Luke 21:5-36**
*5 And as some spake of **the temple**, how it was adorned with goodly stones and gifts, he said,

6 As for these things which ye behold, **the days will come, in the which there shall not be left one stone upon another, that shall not be thrown down**.

7 And they asked him, saying, Master, but **when** shall these things be? and **what sign will there be** when these things shall come to pass?

8 And he said, **Take heed that ye be not deceived**: for many shall come in my name, saying, I am Christ; and the time draweth near: go ye not therefore after them.

9 But when ye shall hear of wars and commotions, **be not terrified**: for these things must first come to pass; but the end is not by and by.

10 Then said he unto them, Nation shall rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom:

11 And great earthquakes shall be in divers places, and famines, and pestilences; and fearful sights and great signs shall there be from heaven.

12 But before all these, **they** shall lay their hands on **you**, and persecute **you**, delivering **you** up to the synagogues, and into prisons, being brought before kings and rulers **for my name's sake.**

13 And it shall turn to **you** for a testimony.

14 Settle it therefore in **your** hearts, not to meditate before what **ye** shall answer:

15 For I will give **you** a mouth and wisdom, which all **your** adversaries shall not be able to gainsay nor resist.

16 And **ye** shall be betrayed both by parents, and brethren, and kinsfolks, and friends; and some of **you** shall they cause to be put to death.

17 **And ye shall be hated of all men for my name's sake.**

18 But there shall not an hair of your head perish.

19 In your patience possess ye your souls.

20 And **when ye** shall see Jerusalem compassed with armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.

21 Then let **them** which are in Judaea flee to the mountains; and let **them** which are in the midst of it depart out; and let not **them** that are in the countries enter thereinto.

22 **For these be the days of vengeance, that all things which are written may be fulfilled**.

23 But woe unto **them** that are with child, and to **them** that give suck, in those days! for there shall be great distress in the land, and wrath upon **this people.**

24 **And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations:** and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.

25 And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity; the sea and the waves roaring;

26 Men's hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken.

27 And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.

28 **And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh**.

29 And he spake to them a parable; Behold the fig tree, and all the trees;

30 When they now shoot forth, ye see and know of your own selves that summer is now nigh at hand.

31 **So likewise ye, when ye see these things come to pass, know ye that the kingdom of God is nigh at hand.**

32 Verily I say unto you, This generation shall not pass away, till all be fulfilled.

33 Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.

34 And **take heed to yourselves, lest at any time your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting, and drunkenness, and cares of this life, and so that day come upon you unawares**.

35 For as a snare shall it come on all them that dwell on the face of the whole earth.

36 **Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man.***

The construction of the first Temple by Solomon put me in mind of the destruction of the 2nd Temple, as prophesied by Jesus.

And reading through the end times prophecy contained in what is called the Olivet Discourse, found here in **Luke 21**, and similar teaching in **Matthew 24** and **Mark 13**, you can see the layers of prophecy, both short term and the long term, both as has passed and what is to come.

It really stands out here in **Luke 21** that Jesus is addressing believers, contrasting them ("You," "ye") with the unbelieving Jews ("They," "them"). For believers, tribulation and persecution, both the disciples of that time, brought before the synagogues and rulers and persecuted for His name's sake, and the general understanding that this will be the fate of believers in the end times as well. "You shall" suffer for His name's sake. And never perish, having eternal life. *Be not terrified...In your patience possess ye your souls.*

This is separate from the "days of vengeance," which came upon the Jews in 70AD as well as in the time to come, after the fullness of the Gentiles comes in. When everyone who will get saved has been. After these many signs take place.

And it is the same pattern, the armies compass the city about and the Jews fall by the sword. "They" shall fall and be led away captive.

Many false doctrines claim this was all written to the Jews or that all of this was fulfilled in 70AD and the Roman destruction of Jerusalem and the Temple, but the far reaching implications laid out by Christ shows that this was dual prophecy. Many things had to happen then, and are yet to happen.

Jesus lays out not only the short term, but the understanding that there will be wars and disasters and all manner of tribulation; *when ye shall hear of wars and commotions, be not terrified: for these things must first come to pass; but the end is not by and by.*

By and by means soon. Any minute.

It is also important to recognize that the disciples asked for a sign and the timing of His return, and Jesus provided it to us. He says it is like seeing the budding of a fig tree, that we may recognize the times and the seasons. That we not be caught off guard the way the rest of the world will be.

The day of the Lord only comes upon us unawares if we are *overcharged with surfeiting*, that is consumed with gluttony and covetousness, or with drunkenness, or the cares of this life. Things of the flesh and of the world, and not the spiritual things of God.

The rapture is not "imminent," and Jesus does not come as a thief in the night to those of us who keep watch. Things must come to pass, and we shouldn't be afraid, but ready and watchful.

All who live godly will see tribulation. But not a hair on our head will perish. We have eternal life.

And when Jesus returns, it will be *with power and great glory.* Everyone will know and see it. It won't be secret. And we who are saved shall rejoice;

*And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.*

Amen

teachings.summary: Reads 2 Thessalonians 2 and 1 Thessalonians 4 to show that prophetic events must occur before the gathering together unto Christ.

John MacArthur has said nothing more prophetically needs to occur for the rapture to happen.

Remember ye not, that, when I was yet with you, I told you these things?And now ye know what withholdeth that he might be revealed in his time. And then shall that Wicked be revealed, whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming: Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders,*

teachings.title: Jesus is the Temple
teachings.summary: Answers the claim of a rebuilt third temple by saying Jesus is the Temple and the church built on the gospel are its pillars.
teachings.text:
“God came in 70 A.D. and did what...? Destroyed the temple. But there’s coming a day, beloved,
in the future when God is going to send the Messiah back to rebuild the temple.”- damned viper, John MacArthur

Jesus IS the Temple, the Lord God Almighty is the Temple. The church built upon the truth of the Gospel, that Jesus is Christ, are the pillars of that Temple.

There is no new, physical 3rd temple built in Jerusalem for "the Jews," that is of Jesus. If one is built, it is for Satan, and for that man of perdition to declare himself God in.

teachings.title: The kingdom of heaven and the kingdom of God
teachings.summary: Sets Daniel 2:44, Matthew 4, Mark 1 and Luke 17 side by side to show the kingdom of heaven and the kingdom of God are one and the same.
teachings.text:
**Daniel 2:44**
*And in the days of these kings shall **the God of heaven set up a kingdom**, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever.*

**Matthew 4:17 **
*From that time Jesus began to preach, and to say, Repent: for **the kingdom of heaven** is at hand.*

**Mark 1:15 **
*And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.*

**Luke 17:20-21**
*And when he was demanded of the Pharisees, when **the kingdom of God** should come, he answered them and said, The kingdom of God cometh not with observation: Neither shall they say, Lo here! or, lo there! for, behold, **the kingdom of God** is within you.*

**Luke 13:28-29**
*There shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth, when ye shall see Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, and all the prophets, **in the kingdom of God**, and you yourselves thrust out. And they shall come from the east, and from the west, and from the north, and from the south, and shall sit down in **the kingdom of God.***

**Matthew 8:11-12**
*And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, **in the kingdom of heaven**. But the children of the kingdom shall be cast out into outer darkness: there shall be weeping and gnashing of teeth.*

There's no way a saved Christian can read these verses and come to the conclusion that they are two separate things.

The only way they can come to that conclusion is if some false prophet told them so.

teachings.title: Preterism, amillennialism and contending for the faith
teachings.summary: Says preterism and amillennialism are signs of a wrong gospel or of a babe in Christ carried about by every wind of doctrine, and cites Jude on contending for the faith.
teachings.text:
Preterism and amillennialism are signs of either believing in vain with the wrong gospel, or in some circumstances, being a babe in Christ *tossed to and fro, and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the sleight of men, and cunning craftiness, whereby they lie in wait to deceive*. Taken away by confident sounding men, rather than Biblical teachings.

*Beloved, when I gave all diligence to write unto you of the common salvation, it was needful for me to write unto you, and exhort you that ye should earnestly contend for the faith which was once delivered unto the saints. For there are certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation, ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into lasciviousness, and denying the only Lord God, and our Lord Jesus Christ. **I will therefore put you in remembrance, though ye once knew this, how that the Lord, having saved the people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed them that believed not..**..But these speak evil of those things which they know not: but what they know naturally, as brute beasts, in those things they corrupt themselves. Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core. These are spots in your feasts of charity, when they feast with you, feeding themselves without fear: clouds they are without water, carried about of winds; trees whose fruit withereth, without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots; Raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, to whom is reserved the blackness of darkness for ever. And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, the Lord cometh with ten thousands of his saints, To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds which they have ungodly committed, and of all their hard speeches which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.

These are murmurers, complainers, walking after their own lusts; and their mouth speaketh great swelling words, having men's persons in admiration because of advantage. But, beloved, remember ye the words which were spoken before of the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ; How that they told you there should be mockers in the last time, who should walk after their own ungodly lusts. These be they who separate themselves, sensual, having not the Spirit. But ye, beloved, building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Ghost, Keep yourselves in the love of God, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ **unto eternal life**.*

teachings.title: Rapture anxiety and the pre-trib leaven
teachings.summary: Argues that the pre-tribulation rapture teaching feeds a weekly fear in children and congregants, while the biblical order of end times and secure salvation brings peace.
teachings.text:
There is an apostasy movement happening in evangelical circles that primarily focuses on normalizing sodomites and promoting feminism as a reaction to "religious trauma." It teaches a false and warped view of the gospel, that "Jesus is love," and so whatever you do that makes you "happy" is good. These "nu-Evangelicals" hold the Bible to be imperfect, that much of its teachings no longer apply, or were the opinions of "misogynists" and "homophobes" like Paul.

They use a mix of genuine failure in their churches, and their own inventions of evil to rationalize their falling away. One of their primary excuses is something called "Rapture Anxiety," and the cause, they say, is the teaching of the heretical doctrine of the Pre-tribulation Rapture. The imminent return of Christ taught by most mainline evangelicals in America today. The primary doctrine of dispensationalism.

While we should note it is their own wicked hearts that has led them to this error, and the itching ears yearning for feel good doctrines from reprobates who have crept in unawares, turning aside to vain jangling, there is a basis of truth to the complaint.

When a church goes all in on a false doctrine, that cannot be justified by scripture, but only through what amounts to gaslighting, it has an effect. When the doctrine teaches different gospels, different "dispensations," and that the church itself is a failure, due to be replaced by the Jews at any moment, it has an effect. Especially among children raised in it. Add to that the rise of "Lordship salvation," "Repent-of-your-sins" heresy and the holier than thou attitudes these bring, and it is no wonder that many fall for this satanic movement. The church having had a bad report. Lying and dissembling about scripture, and, because they teach a "fruit inspector" mentality, they inevitably fall into cover-ups and hypocrisy. They become respecters of persons, and make excuses for those that are elders, tithe more, volunteer more, etc, while condemning those who they judge are worse sinners than themselves. Who will be "Left Behind" if they don't get right. Heresy begetting damnable heresy. The leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy, enters a church and corrupts it over time.

Pre-trib rapture is leaven. The idea that nothing matters, that any moment you can be caught up to heaven and so you'll never experience tribulation, appeals to older congregants, but is terrifying to children who aren't secure in the gospel, because they are taught a confusing message of faith plus works. Who are told week after week that "At any moment, maybe before the end of this service, Christ might return!" Doomsday prophets, setting dates on charts are bad enough. But when that date is always "Now!" it becomes a weekly trauma.

Biblical end times prophesy, the teaching of the rapture being after tribulation, after a falling away, after certain undeniable signs, the man of sin being revealed, etc...is meant to teach us patience and longsuffering. It is hopeful, and should increase our faith. The security of salvation by grace through faith making those that believe understand they are secure, sealed by the Spirit unto redemption tied with the understanding that that redemption may be well after our natural lifetime, leaves the believer in peace.

The knowledge that the church isn't a "plan B," but the only plan for salvation, and the gospel being true, not changing for different people and eras, is meant to be a comfort, not a terror. Knowing we have already overcome the world in Christ. The peace that passes all understanding.

It would be the height of irony if Dispensationalism was the seed of the great apostasy, the "falling away."

teachings.title: The day of the Lord is darkness to the damned
teachings.summary: Quotes Amos 5:18 to show that the day of the Lord is darkness and not light for those who desire it without God. Says believers are of the day and the light, and that day and night are a picture of this, a parable of creation.
teachings.text:
What ends do the damned have on the day of the Lord? They get darkness. Sun and moon and stars.

We are of the day and of the light.

In fact one of the reasons God created day and night, if not the only reason, perhaps. It's a picture of this very thing at the end. That we understand the night and the day, the darkness and the light.

So we have that understanding when we hear God's word say it, we can picture it, and in picturing it understand what God's saying. The parable of creation

teachings.title: Primary doctrines before prophecy
teachings.summary: Notes people who spend years decoding end times prophecy from the works of men yet do not understand the basic gospel. Says much of prophecy, especially the timing, is fairly easy to understand once first things and secondary doctrines are in place.
teachings.text:
There are people who spend years researching and debating end times Bible prophecy, going through works of men to try and decode the order of things, and yet have no understanding of the basic Gospel of salvation, or any of the primary doctrines of God.

I have run in to such people repeatedly for decades. They can't accept the truth and insist there are secrets to learn and mysteries to unravel that cannot be answered in scripture, but could be by some obscure work.

While there are some things unclear, seen through a glass darkly, much of it is fairly easy to understand, the timing of things most of all. In the spirit and understanding of first things and secondary doctrines reveal a lot of it. Especially being able to clear up misconception and false teaching and wild theories.

teachings.title: Luke 21 and the so-called three snares
teachings.summary: Answers a preacher's claim of a secret doctrine of three snares in Luke 21:34, showing that the snare in verse 35 refers back to the day of the Lord. Explains the order of events from Matthew 24, the signs, and why believers who watch will not be caught unawares.
teachings.text:
**Luke 21:33-36**

*33 Heaven and earth shall pass away: but my words shall not pass away.

34 And take heed to yourselves, lest at any time your hearts be overcharged with surfeiting, and drunkenness, and cares of this life, and so **that day** come upon you unawares.

35 For as **a snare** shall it come on all them that dwell on the face of the whole earth.

36 Watch ye therefore, and pray always, that ye may be accounted worthy to escape all these things that shall come to pass, and to stand before the Son of man.*

This caught my attention scrolling through Telegram, and because I wasn't certain what he was talking about by these so-called "three snares," I watched a little bit of the video.

Wiles claims that Luke 21:34 seems as if it is a non sequitur, that Jesus in talking about the end times throws this bit about surfeiting, drunkenness and cares of this life in to his preaching, and that these are the secret "three snares" that all Christians must avoid if they want to go to heaven when Jesus' second coming is here.

Rick Wiles and his co-host, Doc Burkhart further say they've never heard anyone else who claims to be an end times prophecy expert mention this doctrine Wiles "discovered." And they chastise viewers who don't "buy and read books" that could explain the "mysteries of Revelation" to them. He then hocks the second edition of his own book.

That's all within the first 5 minutes.

(Just to be clear for those wondering, surfeiting is a word that means being full of something that you've overindulged in)

When we turn to the actual chapter and verse in question, we see that the snare that is referred to in verse 35, refers back up to "that day," meaning the day of the Lord. The second coming, after the tribulation in those days, where the dead in Christ are risen and called up into the clouds, followed by the living who are saved at that time, caught up with Jesus, and the wrath of God begins being poured out for the next three and a half years.

Jesus has just finished telling the apostles exactly the order of events, and how it will play out. We see the same account in Matthew 24. Jesus tells them, and us, that we will know that the time is growing close. We will see the signs. His coming will not be a surprise to those of us who are paying attention and who are studying his word and praying because all of those other things will have come to pass leading up to it. There are three and a half years of Great tribulation on Earth with the Antichrist and the persecution of the saints. He tells the parable of the fig tree, to draw a comparison to how you know what season it is based on these observations. Jesus warning about not being so full of the cares of this world, caught up and drunkenness, caught up in a form of worldly gluttony, so that we are able to pay attention to those signs and, that's not be caught unawares. Because it's to the unsaved that his coming will be like a thief in the night. That carnal Christians who are backslidden and not keeping their mind towards God, will also be taken by surprise, potentially.

Wiles turns this into some kind of weird works-based doctrine that if you're unhealthy, be it gluttony, drunk or a worry wart, you won't get saved when Jesus returns.

teachings.title: Revelation was written after 70 AD
teachings.summary: Argues that Revelation was written around 96 AD, after the destruction of Jerusalem, so Nero was not the antichrist. Notes that the emperors of that time were comparatively lenient and that none of this matches the end times prophecy or the second coming, which is still to come.
teachings.text:
I don't know who needs to hear this but Revelation was written sometime around 96 CE, 30+ years after the destruction of Jerusalem, scattering of the remnant of Jews, and Nero, who died in 68AD wasn't *the* antichrist.

Carry on

teachings.title: The abomination of desolation and the image of the beast
teachings.summary: Considers the view that the abomination of desolation and the image of the beast in Revelation 13:15 may be a form of self-aware AI set up in the temple by the beast. Notes that the prophecy has dual fulfilment and does not fit Antiochus or Titus alone.
teachings.text:
Speaking of AI, there are some who believe that the "abomination of desolation" spoken of by Jesus and prophesied by Daniel will be some form of semi-sentient AI, set up in the temple in Jerusalem by the beast after the Jews who help being the antichrist to power are betrayed, and the days of vengeance wipe most of them out.

Jerusalem then desolate, we'll see the beast set himself up as God in the temple and the abomination he puts there in the desolation could be some form of self-aware AI. That it is the "image of the beast" that is made alive (given breath) and speaks (**Revelation 13:15** And he had power to give life unto the image of the beast, that the image of the beast should both speak, and cause that as many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed.)

(The false idea that the abomination of desolation is only referring to Antiochus, whose blasphemous declaration that he was "god manifest" and desecration of the 2nd temple couldn't be correct, as that was well before Jesus Christ earthly ministry, and the interpretation that it was Titus and the destruction of 70AD doesn't align with the prophecy in Daniel. As with most end times prophecy, there is dual fulfilment and echos of the events of the end times that we see reverberating back through time)

teachings.title: Matthew 24:22 and the pre-trib rapture
teachings.summary: Reads Matthew 24:19-22 and asks why the days would be shortened for the elect if the saved were raptured before them. Calls the pre-tribulation rapture a false doctrine, while saying he does not believe the tribulation is here.
teachings.text:
**Matthew 24**

*19 And woe unto them that are with child, and to them that give suck in those days!
20 But pray ye that your flight be not in the winter, neither on the sabbath day:

21 For then shall be great tribulation, such as was not since the beginning of the world to this time, no, nor ever shall be.

22 And except those days should be shortened, there should no flesh be saved: but for the elect's sake those days shall be shortened*.

teachings.title: The Antichrist deceives the lost, not the saved
teachings.summary: Corrects the idea that saved Christians will be deceived by the Antichrist, from 2 Thessalonians 2: those deceived are those who received not the love of the truth. Adds that name-only Christians are likely to be his biggest supporters.
teachings.text:
This is a category error. Those being deceived aren't saved Christians. The Antichrist does not deceive believers, but those who dwell in inequity.
