**2 Thessalonians 2**
*7 For the mystery of iniquity doth already work: only he who now letteth will let, until he be taken out of the way.

8 And then shall that Wicked be revealed, whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming:

9 Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders,

10 And with all deceivableness of unrighteousness in them that perish; because they received not the love of the truth, that they might be saved.

11 And for this cause God shall send them strong delusion, that they should believe a lie:

12 That they all might be damned who believed not the truth, but had pleasure in unrighteousness.*

Of course, this doesn't mean Evangelicals and Catholics and other sects that are ostensibly Christian, but in name only, can't be deceived. In fact, they are highly likely to be, as they aren't believers on Christ and saved by faith. If anything, they will be the biggest supporters of the Antichrist when he gains power.

teachings.title: Counted as sheep for the slaughter
teachings.summary: The lament of Psalm 44 is turned into instruction in Romans 8 that nothing can separate us from Christ's love, and believers grown weak by comfort must be prepared to endure persecution, even the coming tribulation, without losing faith.
teachings.text:
**1 Peter 4:12–14**
*Beloved, think it not strange concerning the fiery trial which is to try you, as though some strange thing happened unto you: But rejoice, inasmuch as ye are partakers of Christ’s sufferings; that, when his glory shall be revealed, ye may be glad also with exceeding joy. If ye be reproached for the name of Christ, happy are ye; for the spirit of glory and of God resteth upon you: on their part he is evil spoken of, but on your part he is glorified.*

If the people who call themselves by His name we're naturally like Stephen, standing up for the faith and being willing to suffer death for the truth while forgiving those that stoned him to death, the New Testament wouldn't be so full of warnings and encouragement.

In **Psalm 44:22–24** they cry out desperately to God;
*Yea, for thy sake are we killed all the day long; we are counted as sheep for the slaughter. Awake, why sleepest thou, O Lord? arise, cast us not off for ever. Wherefore hidest thou thy face, and forgettest our affliction and our oppression?*

The same lament is turned to edifying instruction in the New Testament;

**Romans 8:35–37**
*Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? shall tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword? As it is written, For thy sake we are killed all the day long; we are accounted as sheep for the slaughter. Nay, in all these things we are more than conquerors through him that loved us.*

Because man is naturally going to complain in the best of times, we need to be prepared for the proper attitude in the worst. To be persuaded that nothing can separate us from the love of Christ. Even when things are bleak.

Jesus Himself gave this encouragement to the church in Smyrna, who were facing real persecution at the hands of their enemies.

**Revelation 2:8–11**
*And unto the angel of the church in Smyrna write; These things saith the first and the last, which was dead, and is alive; I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich) and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan. Fear none of those things which thou shalt suffer: behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days: be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life. He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death.*

Just as the instructions to live separated lives, to be holy as He is holy, is necessary because man does not by his fleshly nature do good works, even those who are saved, the same flesh tends to need reminders of past victory, while still may cry out "Why?" to their Saviour.

Righteous Job did. The best man of his generation, and yet he sought answers from God, and sinned not with his mouth while doing so, according to scripture.

Modern American Christians, made weak by the comforts and bounty God has graciously given our nation, grown fat off His blessings, will most assuredly cry out the same laments when the abomination of desolation is rolled out, and the armies of the beast strike us down.

Even the spirits of the martyrs in Great Tribulation will cry out, impatiently.

**Revelation 6:9–10**
*And when he had opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of them that were slain for the word of God, and for the testimony which they held: And they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?*

We naturally may feel abandoned in the thick of it. Crying out, as the congregation does, is sadly expected.

*Awake, why sleepest thou, O Lord? arise, cast us not off for ever. Wherefore hidest thou thy face, and forgettest our affliction and our oppression?*

We may be beaten down, bowed to the dust, despondent.

teachings.title: I shall be satisfied when I awake with thy likeness
teachings.summary: God keeps His children under His wing, and our satisfaction is in the resurrection when we shall see Christ and be like Him, whatever the wicked gain now.
teachings.text:
Continuing in **Psalms 17**, we see that David's importunity comes from his faith in God to hear those who call upon Him. That we may go boldly before the throne of grace, because He has shown us that He listens to our cries. The initial call for salvation in the Lord's name gives us the hope that He listens to us for far less important matters, such as our suffering in this life.

The Lord's lovingkindness is already apparent to those that put their trust in Him, that have been saved by His strong right-hand. Christ Jesus. We know that our Savior is at the right hand of the Father. The New Testament is clear on this. But David is writing hundreds of years earlier, showing that Old Testament saints knew and understood the concept, even if they didn't have the full revelation and details.

*Keep me as the apple of the eye, hide me under the shadow of thy wings, From the wicked that oppress me, from my deadly enemies, who compass me about.*

Keep me, o Lord. It is His power that keeps the children of God under His protection and secure in His promises. We shall not fear, because we are under His mighty wing, as a mother hen keeps her chicks.

Jesus laments the unfaithful Jews for refusing to be gathered thus.

**Matthew 23:37–39**
*O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not! Behold, your house is left unto you desolate. For I say unto you, Ye shall not see me henceforth, till ye shall say, Blessed is he that cometh in the name of the Lord*.

And His protection is needed in this world, where they hate us for His holy name. Where we are often at the mercy of forces beyond our reckoning. Where the judgment of God against our nation is executed by the hands of the wicked. They are His sword.

They may profit in this life. They may have riches, while we are poor. They may have children and an inheritance. But we have the eternal promise of Christ, which is far more precious than any treasure of this life.

*As for me, I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness.*

This is the eternal perspective that Christians should seek. That our satisfaction is in the resurrection, and the current, temporal troubles are nothing compared to the everlasting.

When we awake, when we are raised up, we will see Jesus, the express likeness of God. But, maybe David is also speaking of the glorified body we will receive in His likeness.

**1 John 3:1–2**
*Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God: therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not. Beloved, now are we the sons of God, and it doth not yet appear what we shall be: but we know that, when he shall appear, we shall be like him; for we shall see him as he is.*

This is our blessed hope. To awake into glory with Him. When we see Jesus as sons of God. Gathered up to the Lord, and with Him shall we ever be.

Ultimately, this is the only satisfaction we need. If our enemies prosper, if God allows them to have advantage over us, while we suffer them, we know His grace is sufficient. That ultimately, vengeance will be His. That in the Lord's love for us, we will see Him as He is, and be like Him.

That no matter what may come in this life, we have peace in the next. Amen

teachings.title: Read it for yourself
teachings.summary: Warns that studying other people's theology and hermeneutics is easier than reading the text yourself, and that eschatology should be read from scripture rather than a prepackaged outline.
teachings.text:
Part of the problem is laziness. Too many Christians, including pastors and professors study to learn theology and hermeneutics, and to understand what other people have interpreted, because it is "easier" than just reading it for yourself.

Eschatology can seem daunting, but if someone hands you a prepackaged outline and charts, you can just adopt it as your own.

The same with soteriologies like Calvinism. (Although this is harder to pull off if a student is already saved and has a firm understanding of the gospel).

In the end, many believers are no better off than Catholics who trust in a "magistrum" to interpret and tell them what the Bible says.

*Prove all things; hold fast that which is good...Study to shew thyself approved unto God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth. *

Search the scriptures to see if the things being taught are so. Don't blindly accept them because of authority or traditions.

teachings.title: Allegories, parables and dogmatic literalism
teachings.summary: Says a major source of heresy is taking allegories, parables and pictures in scripture and applying a dogmatic literalism to them.
teachings.text:
Probably the biggest source of heresy is the tendency to take allegories and parables and pictures of things given by God in His word that we can have better understanding, and applying a dogmatic literalism to them. Even conflicting images using similar terms about different topics become standardized to support a doctrine that is not necessarily being taught.

This creates presuppositional terms that shut down thought.

Terms like elect, repent, the church, the bride, the wedding supper, Abraham's bosom, Jacob's trouble, and others lead to a drastic misunderstanding at best and foolish heresy at worse.

Rather than allowing the Bible to explain itself in the context, people plug in their own ideas and systematics, usually that they have learned from others and adopted unquestionably.

Once they've been adopted, proof texting becomes a substitute for exegesis. And so every instance needs to be conformed to the pre-existing idea instead of just hearing what God's saying.

teachings.title: The King's wedding procession and many crowns
teachings.summary: The bride's search pictures the empty tomb and finding Christ, and Solomon's procession pictures Christ returning with His saints for the marriage supper and His kingdom.
teachings.text:
Chapter 3 begins with the woman waking to a desolate bed, unable to find her beloved. Seeking him, she desperately searches in the night, throughout the city streets. She repeats the refrain that she *sought him, but I found him not.*

She then encounters the night watch, and enquires of them if they had seen *him, whom my soul loveth.*

This passage beautifully reflects the death of Christ, picturing the panicked feeling of believers at His death, and at the empty tomb. The watchmen, the religious leaders who crucified Him, unable to give an answer, but then, in her search, she finds him. *Him whom my soul loveth.*

And she holds him and will not let him go, bringing him into her mother's house, even to the bed chamber she was conceived in. As Jesus comes into us, and is held in the most intimate chamber of our hearts.

For the second time in the song, the chorus in verse 5, also found in chapter 2:7 is repeated:

*I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please*.

It is repeated again in chapter 8, and the verse is used as transition in the structure of the song.

While it may picture the current time, where we wait for our beloved, the Lord Jesus to return, it also serves as an oath, asking the daughters of Jerusalem to swear by the roes and hinds, the graceful and skittish deer of the land, to not stir the Beloved too early. To let him sleep as late as he pleases.

The immediate application speaks to the delicate nature of love, especially in its earliest stages, where you almost feel a surreal and magical experience and are afraid it could burst like a bubble at any time. You don't want to lose that joyous state. You don't want it to be disturbed, like the gazelles of the mountains startled at a sudden movement or sound.

She has found her beloved and taken him into her heart, and wants that joy of her salvation to last.

The chorus serves to transition the narrative to an epic description of the King, and his entourage, emerging from the wilderness like pillars of smoke, an endless caravan. Perfumed and decked out in fine clothes for the wedding.

This pictures the return of Christ, after the wrath, on a white horse with ten thousands of His saints, wearing their wedding clothes, prepared for the marriage supper of the Lamb.

The bed of the King, his chariot, surrounded by threescore valiant men, the valiant of Israel. The soldiers with swords at their hip, like the prophets armed with the word of God.

King Solomon's chariot, made of the finest wood, decked in silver and gold, covered in royal purple, and as it goes, *paved with love*, *for the daughters of Jerusalem*. This is the interior of the royal chariot, embroidery made by the daughters of the land with love, the inner bed, where the King and his bride would recline.

The purity of God in the silver pillars, His grace, the gold that surrounds us. The purple of His majesty as Lord, and the interior, the soft comfort of His love for us.

The bride of the song calls out for the daughters of Zion, Jerusalem, to go out and welcome the King. To examine his wedding crown, to celebrate the betrothal and his gladness. The tradition of the people is that the mother of the bridegroom crafts a crown to celebrate the nuptials. Not a crown of royalty, but of love.

In **Revelation 19:12**, as Christ rides forth to claim ultimate victory and gather His people, the text says, *on his head were many crowns*.

The crowns of Christ at His triumphant arrival to meet the descending New Jerusalem, adorned as a bride, are the diadem of His love for His beloved, just as Solomon's love for his bride.

As John writes in *Revelation 21:2*:
*And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.*

The allegory and picture of the King of Kings arriving at His wedding feast, at the culmination of history, to usher in His millennial Kingdom, reflected in the prophetic love song written by Solomon.

teachings.title: Rise up, my love, and come away
teachings.summary: The bride waiting for her beloved pictures believers waiting for Christ's return to gather His elect, while the wicked hide in the rocks from the wrath of the Lamb.
teachings.text:
Chapter 2 contains a poetic back and forth dialogue between the woman and the man, the rose of Sharon and her beloved, an apple tree among the trees of the wood. He compares other women to thorns, but she is a lily, a beautiful flower among them.

The woman delights in his shade, his protection, and in his fruit, which is sweet to her taste. He calls her to his banquet, under the banner of love.

Again, we see the gospel. He is the tree of life, over a precious flower among the thorns. Invited to the banquet house of the Lord. The wedding supper of the Lamb.

She is overcome by his love, she longs for him as we long for Jesus, and His embrace in that great day of redemption.

 *I charge you, O ye daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, and by the hinds of the field, that ye stir not up, nor awake my love, till he please.*

The timing of the Lord's return is at God's pleasure. Just as she waits for her love to awake, we patiently wait for Him to return.

The roes, the hinds of the field are the wild deer that play in the pastures and roam the hills and mountains.

She hears the voice of her beloved, and compares him to the roebuck leaping and skipping on mountains and hills. She sees him through the lattice of the window, just beyond her walls, and he speaks to her, calling her to rise up and come with him.

This pictures the return of Christ, gathering the elect from the four corners of the world. Jesus descends with a shout. We who are His hear His voice, and Rise up, and come away with Him.

*For, lo, the winter is past, the rain is over and gone;* it is spring. The rains fall and the flowers burst forth, and a time of peace is at hand. The signs of the season are showing. The fig tree puts forth her green figs.

**Matthew 24:32–33**
*Now learn a parable of the fig tree; When his branch is yet tender, and putteth forth leaves, ye know that summer is nigh: So likewise ye, when ye shall see all these things, know that it is near, even at the doors.*

She begs to see her love, he is among the clefts of the rock, the stairs of the mountains, as a dove, his face is upon those that take shelter from His wrath there. They fear him. But she longs to see him.

**Revelation 6:15–17**
*And the kings of the earth, and the great men, and the rich men, and the chief captains, and the mighty men, and every bondman, and every free man, hid themselves in the dens and in the rocks of the mountains; And said to the mountains and rocks, Fall on us, and hide us from the face of him that sitteth on the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb: For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand?*

*Take us the foxes, the little foxes, that spoil the vines: for our vines have tender grapes.* The wrath is upon these "little foxes," the wicked, those that spoil and corrupt the tender grapes. The wicked that seek to destroy the believers, especially during the great tribulation.

Her certainty of their love, that he is hers and she is his, even as he waits for his time, reflects the eternal security we have as believers in Christ. Waiting patiently for His return, when the day breaks and the shadows flee the light.

teachings.title: Remember thy Creator before it is too late
teachings.summary: Solomon's conclusion that all is vanity calls men to remember their Creator now, before death or the darkened sun of the day of the Lord, when it will be too late to fear Him.
teachings.text:
The end of Solomon's sermon, the preacher has spoken. Life is vanity and vexation of spirit, man toils and dies. There is iniquity and wickedness. Time and chance. A time for every purpose under Heaven. No guarantee of tomorrow. Only fleeting moments of joy where God has blessed us to enjoy the fruits of our labor. We should rejoice in our youth and remember the darkness, reflecting in mourning more than reveling in mirth. We should seek wisdom and reject foolishness, and in all things remember that there is a God, and He is just in His judgment.

And so, Solomon the king and preacher, with his thousands of proverbs, songs and sayings (and wives), sums up the end of the matter. Remember thy Creator. Remember Him in your youth, while it is still light. Before the darkness of this life or the time to come, when it is too late and tribulations and tragedies bring grief and sorrow. Before you die, and it's too late.

Before the day of the Lord.

The sun and the moon and the stars darkening is always a sign of the end, and the 2nd coming of Christ.

**Matthew 24:29-32**
*Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken: And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of man coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory. And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.*

**Joel 2:31**
*The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the great and terrible day of the Lord come.*

There is a time it is too late to fear the Lord, to get right with Him, to remember our Creator.

**2 Corinthians 6:2**
*(For he saith, I have heard thee in a time accepted, and in the day of salvation have I succoured thee: behold, now is the accepted time; behold, now is the day of salvation.)*

The day of the Lord will see the keepers of the house tremble and the strong men bow, every knee shall bow and tongue confess. The rich men and rulers will beg the rocks and mountains to fall upon them. They shall have their fear come upon them. The music will cease. The streets full of mourning.

**Revelation 6:17**
*For the great day of his wrath is come; and who shall be able to stand?*

The grinders shall cease, for there are few...

**Matthew 24:41-42**
*Two women shall be grinding at the mill; the one shall be taken, and the other left. Watch therefore: for ye know not what hour your Lord doth come.*

The day of our death or the day of the Lord, the end comes for all men.

*Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern*.

If our bodies are broken, our spine snapped, our skull cracked, our heart stops and we bleed out, if our body can no longer move...And ever the curse of Adam is upon us;

*Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.*

**Genesis 3:19**
*In the sweat of thy face shalt thou eat bread, till thou return unto the ground; for out of it wast thou taken: for dust thou art, and unto dust shalt thou return.*

...All things considered, this is the ultimate vanity. *Vanity of vanities, saith the preacher; all is vanity.*

The preacher is wise. The wisest man in history, filled with the Spirit of God to know things and the time and treasure to consider all the ways of man under the Sun. He sought understanding and set in order many proverbs, and taught the people knowledge. Seeking truth. Instruction in uprightness. Righteousness.

*The words of the wise are as goads, and as nails fastened by the masters of assemblies, which are given from one shepherd.*

teachings.title: Dispensationalism and pre-trib as a shibboleth
teachings.summary: Says dispensationalism and the pre-trib rapture have become tests of orthodoxy in independent churches, but urges submitting to a sound pastor since the right gospel, Bible and soul winning matter most.
teachings.text:
The introduction of dispensationalism and the error of pre-trib rapture has become a defining shibboleth, making what are supposed to be Independent churches into a quasi-denomination through perverse incentives to enforce orthodoxy on these secondary doctrines.

This is how heresy becomes entrenched. It is how the early churches that broke off fellowship to do baby baptism eventually formed the Catholic denomination. Then Orthodox split over how the baptism was performed, not the error of it. Protestants split over corruption in the Roman Church, not the errors, and became their own denominations.

The strength of the IFB should be their allegiance to Christ and the fundamentals of the word over networking and finances. But error needs to use perverse incentives to protect it, because it can't stand up to scriptural rebuke.

This shouldn't dissuade you from going to the best local, independent, fundamental Baptist Church you can find in your area. Pastor Awes is correct; What matters is the right gospel, the right Bible, soul-winning. A brother can be wrong on the timing of the gathering of the elect. We should submit to the pastor and not seek to sow discord among the brethren.

But, we can also lovingly point out the hypocrisy of this system when appropriate.

teachings.title: Assurance and the perseverance promise
teachings.summary: Says believers can be assured they will never perish, and that enduring to the end in the Gospels is a promise for those living through the tribulation, not about spiritual salvation.
teachings.text:
"Believers in Christ can be personally assured that they WILL NEVER PERISH FOREVER because their salvation rests solely upon the faithfulness and finished work of the Savior on their behalf."

So true. **Believers** in Christ have that blessed assurance. People who believe in vain and depart from the faith never believed in the first place, and don't have that assurance.

"Perseverance of the saints" has nothing to do with spiritual salvation or anything else regarding the gospel. It's a promise made by Jesus to people who are alive during tribulation that if they endure to the end of that tribulation, they will be saved out of it by the coming of the Lord.

Heretics and fools twist the meaning to apply it to the gospel. They hate the word of God and have to take things wildly out of context to try and make their foolish and unbiblical arguments.

teachings.title: Not by might, but by my Spirit
teachings.summary: Zechariah's golden candlestick fed by two olive trees shows that the temple is restored by God's Spirit, with lamp oil picturing the Holy Ghost, the olive trees the two witnesses of Revelation, and the candlesticks the churches.
teachings.text:
We are in **Zechariah 4** and the prophet is visited by an angel and a vision, as out of a deep sleep. He sees a golden candle stick with 7 candles, fed by oil from a bowl, with pipes from 2 olive trees beside it. Confused the prophet asks what it is he is being shown.

This is pictured in the instructions for the Tabernacle;

**Exodus 25:31-37**
*And thou shalt make a candlestick of pure gold: of beaten work shall the candlestick be made: his shaft, and his branches, his bowls, his knops, and his flowers, shall be of the same. And six branches shall come out of the sides of it; three branches of the candlestick out of the one side, and three branches of the candlestick out of the other side: Three bowls made like unto almonds, with a knop and a flower in one branch; and three bowls made like almonds in the other branch, with a knop and a flower: so in the six branches that come out of the candlestick. And in the candlesticks shall be four bowls made like unto almonds, with their knops and their flowers. And there shall be a knop under two branches of the same, and a knop under two branches of the same, and a knop under two branches of the same, according to the six branches that proceed out of the candlestick. Their knops and their branches shall be of the same: all it shall be one beaten work of pure gold. And thou shalt make the seven lamps thereof: and they shall light the lamps thereof, that they may give light over against it.*

**Exodus 27:20-21**
*And thou shalt command the children of Israel, that they bring thee pure oil olive beaten for the light, to cause the lamp to burn always. In the tabernacle of the congregation without the vail, which is before the testimony, Aaron and his sons shall order it from evening to morning before the Lord: it shall be a statute for ever unto their generations on the behalf of the children of Israel.*

In the Bible, such as the Parable of the Ten Virgins (**Matthew 25**), lamp oil is a symbol of the Holy Spirit and spiritual preparedness. Here it is the same, the word of the Lord unto Zerubbabel, that it is by God's Spirit he shall restore the temple and Jerusalem.

The candles are described as being fed continuously by the two olive trees, so filled with oil they pipe it out to fill the bowls directly from their branches. Without a press and refinement. Pure.

In Revelation we learn that the two olive trees that are before the Lord, are the two witnesses. Two great men of God who give prophecy, by the word of God.

There are theories as to who these two men are. Many say Moses and Elijah, those who stood glorified with Christ on the mount of transfiguration. Others believe Elijah and Enoch, both taken up into Heaven, translated without death.

But it would make sense that either way, the continuous light of God's word, fed with the oil of His Spirit, would be upon the rebuilding of the Temple. Where Zerubbabel had laid a foundation but hadn't completed it yet.

The candles themselves represent the Spirit of God upon churches. Upon the house of God.

**Revelation 1:18-20**
*I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death. Write the things which thou hast seen, and the things which are, and the things which shall be hereafter; The mystery of the seven stars which thou sawest in my right hand, and the seven golden candlesticks. The seven stars are the angels of the seven churches: and the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven churches.*

The 7 candles are also tied to the 7 Spirits of the Lord;

**Revelation 1:4**
*John to the seven churches which are in Asia: Grace be unto you, and peace, from him which is, and which was, and which is to come; and from the seven Spirits which are before his throne;*

**Isaiah 11:2**
*And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord*

teachings.title: Read Old Testament prophecy through the New
teachings.summary: Differences between OT and NT prophecy are what could have been versus what will be, so we should scrap Darby and Scofield and read the OT through the NT.
teachings.text:
And so the implications of this Theory are broad and deep. It would apply to just about every covenant promise made with conditions to the people of Israel in the Old Testament and any differences between Old Testament prophecy of end times and New.

Ezekiel's Battle of Gog and Magog has some different aspects to it than Revelation's. They still happen, As described by John from the Revelation given him, and the difference is what could have been versus what will be now that the Old Testament is done away with. Necessary changes.

The millennial Kingdom references in Old Testament prophecy very slightly from what we are clearly taught in the new New Testament.

All of the little nuances and seeming contradictions and places where people trying to rightly divide the word of God are jamming Square pegs into round holes to make the prophecies we are given in the New Testament fit with the promises given in the Old.

One of the evils of dispensationalism is that it has so badly blinded everyone, but even we who reject it are so used to dealing with everything on their terms. What if that's just a huge mistake. What if we need to scrap everything that comes out of Darby and Schofield and dispensationalism entirely, and take a new view of the Old Testament through the lens of the New?

teachings.title: The dry bones are the resurrection, not 1948
teachings.summary: The valley of dry bones prophesies the literal resurrection and Christ's kingdom over the Israel of God, and dispensationalists wickedly give these promises to unbelieving Jews by applying them to 1948.
teachings.text:
We are in **Ezekiel 37**, perhaps the most well known passage in the prophetic book, and the preaching of the valley of dry bones.

Them bones, them bones, them dry bones.

It is one of the clearest prophecies of the resurrection and millennial kingdom of believers in the Old Testament. In the second part of the chapter, He has the prophet show two sticks to the people, one Judah, the other Ephraim, or Israel, the Northern Kingdom, and they are miraculously joined in the prophet's hand.

*Thus saith the Lord God; Behold, O my people, I will open your graves, and cause you to come up out of your graves, and bring you into the land of Israel. And ye shall know that I am the Lord, when I have opened your graves, O my people, and brought you up out of your graves, And shall put my spirit in you, and ye shall live*.

Not only shall the graves give up their dead, and risen bodies be made whole, and the winds from the four corners give life, but God says He *shall put my spirit in you, and ye shall live*, and be ruled over as one nation, the Israel of God, under *David, my servant* - Christ Jesus.

Many dispensationalists today will claim this is a prophecy for "the Jews." God says no, He will gather all the people to their land.

They will say this was fulfilled in 1948. John Hagee and Hal Lindsey and other famous dispensationalist Zionists have pushed this idea, repeatedly in their efforts to pervert Christian judgment regarding the modern state claiming to be Israel.

They teach that **Ezekiel 37** and the valley of dry bones prophecy refers to the restoration of Israel in 1948, and falsely interprets the vision as a symbolic representation of the "Jewish people's return to their land after centuries of exile." In this view, the dry bones coming to life signify the physical and national rebirth of Israel, with the reestablishment of the state in 1948 seen as a fulfillment of "God's promise."

One of the most wicked aspects of dispensationalism is that it gives holy promises to believers to unbelieving Jews. It makes firm promises into vague and dark sayings, to justify their false teachings.

The literal resurrection is promised. The Spirit of God indwelling us. The Kingdom of Christ, ruled by Jesus.

Not godless antichrists, who reject Him.

We will be joined as one Kingdom, the Israel of God, made up of believers from Adam through the final Christian saved before the day of the Lord comes. This is a promise to those of us in the New Testament, as much as it was to believers in Ezekiel's day. Amen

teachings.title: We are the righteous remnant
teachings.summary: Believers are the salt that withholds God's judgment, and when the salt loses its savour the remnant will be taken like Lot before His wrath is poured out.
teachings.text:
Beginning in **Isaiah 1**, the major prophecy set in pre-captivity Judea, the Southern Kingdom, Isaiah preached in the 8th century BC, in a similar timeframe as the minor prophets and Kings and Chronicles we have recently covered, and so the themes are familiar.

Israel is gone astray, into adultery with foreign gods, idols, and wickedness. Blood of the innocent shed, the poor defrauded, the widow uncared-for. The sickness of the rulers, even in Judah, has corrupted the Temple as well. God is displeased, and is warning of His coming judgment.

Here, in Isaiah, God is pleading with the people, *Let us reason together*. The Lord has made it clear, from Moses to their present that if they walked in His commandments, they would be His people, and He would be their Lord and the land would be theirs and be blessed.

And yet they fall short, and worse, commit iniquity. Unrighteous judgment. He cannot abide it any longer.

*Except the Lord of hosts had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom, and we should have been like unto Gomorrah.*

This calls back to the pleading of Abraham before Sodom's destruction, that if there were yet ten righteous men, God would spare the city. But it also points to our own time, and the coming judgment.

**Matthew 5:13**
*Ye are the salt of the earth: but if the salt have lost his savour, wherewith shall it be salted? it is thenceforth good for nothing, but to be cast out, and to be trodden under foot of men*.

We are the righteous remnant. Believers are the salt that preserves the earth and withholds God's judgment. We are called to retain that savour, to be faithful and to obey the Lord's commandments, being a light unto the world.

And when the fullness of the nations comes, and the salt loses its savour, a falling away, the small remnant will be taken like Lot, spirited away by the angels of God at Jesus coming. And His wrath will pour out on the unrighteous.

But, as always, God's refining judgment will lead to the redemption of those who trust in Him. The city of righteousness will be ours. That faithful city, Jerusalem the mother of us all.

teachings.title: He that endureth to the end shall be saved
teachings.summary: Enduring to the end is about being saved out of tribulation and persecution, not about keeping eternal life, which cannot be lost.
teachings.text:
Amos continues, calling upon that remnant of Joseph, those who seek the Lord, to hate the evil and love the good, that the Lord God of hosts will be gracious to them in this tribulation.

We need to keep this in mind, ourselves. Things are going to be bad, waxing worse and worse. The patience of the saints, our "enduring to the end," is found in this instruction to hate evil, love good and establish judgement and righteousness.

Too many false teachers assert that perseverance is for our spiritual salvation, that we could lose the free gift of eternal life, but that is not the context or meaning of it. It is for grace and protection during tribulation and persecution.

**Matthew 24:9-13**
*Then shall they deliver you up to be afflicted, and shall kill you: and ye shall be hated of all nations for my name's sake. And then shall many be offended, and shall betray one another, and shall hate one another. And many false prophets shall rise, and shall deceive many. And because iniquity shall abound, the love of many shall wax cold. But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.*

Saved from the persecution. Saved out of great tribulation.

**Revelation 7:14**
*And I said unto him, Sir, thou knowest. And he said to me, These are they which came out of great tribulation, and have washed their robes, and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.*

teachings.title: Faithful servants made rulers in the kingdom
teachings.summary: As David divided roles in his kingdom, the saved will be given duties and rule in the millennial reign according to their faithfulness, so we should use our talents to win others to Christ.
teachings.text:
Much like the division of priests and rulers in the kingdom of David, so too will be the Kingdom of Heaven. And in the millennial reign, we who are saved will be appointed to duties, roles and responsibilities, and even being judge over matters pertaining to God and affairs of the King.

Dedicate your time to taking the talents God has given you, and gaining others to Christ. Strive to be one who on that day, hears the voice of our Savior say, "Well done, good and faithful servant; thou hast been faithful over what's been given you. I will make you ruler over many things."

We shall judge even angels.

And there shall be thrones, cities and wards, areas of responsibility, and gates and roads where a good and faithful servant shall have responsibility, and less fruitful will serve in other capacities to the administration of Christ's Kingdom.

These are the crowns we strive for. This is why we humble ourselves and serve those in need. This is where the least among us, meek and lowly, become first in the Kingdom of God.

teachings.title: The spirit of Josiah, not Hezekiah
teachings.summary: Unlike Hezekiah, content that judgment would not come in his day (the attitude behind the pre-tribulation rapture's appeal), believers should, like Josiah, lament sin and preach against it even facing tribulation.
teachings.text:
*Notwithstanding the Lord turned not from the fierceness of his great wrath, wherewith his anger was kindled against Judah, because of all the provocations that Manasseh had provoked him withal. And the Lord said, I will remove Judah also out of my sight, as I have removed Israel, and will cast off this city Jerusalem which I have chosen, and the house of which I said, My name shall be there.*

The revival and zeal for the Lord shown by King Josiah led God to grant his reign a measure of peace and delayed their judgement against them. But it did not prevent God's wrath from being poured out eventually.

And Josiah knew by the prophecy given to him that the judgment was inevitable. But he still did that which was right and was tearful and full of regret for the evil done in the land by his fathers and the people.

Contrast that with when Hezekiah said unto Isaiah, who had given the same warning; *Good is the word of the Lord which thou hast spoken. And he said, Is it not good, if peace and truth be in my days?*

Hezekiah, a good king as well who did fear the Lord, accepted the judgment and was glad it wasn't in his day, but did not utterly purge the land as Josiah did. He was relieved that the wrath was held back, and that his children would suffer the consequences rather than him.

This mentality is common among what is called the "baby boomer" generation, many of whom recognizing that the consequences for their sin would lead to judgment, took comfort in the fact that they wouldn't be here to see it. And it is no wonder that the false doctrine of a pre-tribulation rapture was so appealing to them.

They rested in the delusion that while the nation may be going to Hell in a hand basket, and that judgment was coming, that they didn't need to worry. They would be spared any trouble when it "got really bad." They didn't make any effort to turn back to the Lord with zeal and lead a revival in hopes of turning back God's wrath or buying more time. They said *Is it not good, if peace and truth be in my days?*

Then you see another generation come, who like Josiah, look to the word of God and understand that the sodomites and the idols and the failure to walk in the statutes of the Lord is the cause of the judgment, and as righteous as God's indignation against us is, we still have a duty to follow His commandments, even if it means facing great tribulation. To lament the wickedness done and to preach and act against it. And to proclaim the word of God and His righteousness to the world. In season or out of season.

It is a different attitude, and one that the old guard of Christians often resent and look down upon, because it convicts them for their inaction, or leads them to special pleading, saying "I tried ...it's not my fault."

I would rather have the spirit of Josiah rending his clothes and seeking after the Lord than of Hezekiah's acquiescence and pride in his earthly wealth.

teachings.title: And so all Israel shall be saved
teachings.summary: All Israel in Romans 11:26 is the true seed adopted by faith, saved through Christ the Deliverer, while partial blindness remains on fleshly Israel until His coming.
teachings.text:
*For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.*

*And so all Israel shall be saved: as it is written, There shall come out of Sion the Deliverer, and shall turn away ungodliness from Jacob: For this is my covenant unto them, when I shall take away their sins.*

Here is the crux of the dispensationalist heresy. Their main proof text. "All Israel shall be saved."

But we know this is not Israel of the flesh. That not all Israel which are of Israel.

*Not as though the word of God hath taken none effect. For they are not all Israel, which are of Israel: Neither, because they are the seed of Abraham, are they all children: but, In Isaac shall thy seed be called. That is, They which are the children of the flesh, these are not the children of God: but the children of the promise are counted for the seed.*

And we see the conditional terms of how all Israel is saved; that a deliverer comes out of Zion, to turn away ungodliness in Jacob. Who will take away their sins.

That is Christ Jesus. The promise is made in and through Him. And so, as it is written, all Israel shall be saved.

The fullness of the Gentiles is the day of redemption. The second coming of Christ Jesus. The day of the Lord. Where the dead in Christ rise and the elect are gathered, and God's wrath is poured out in the unbelieving world.

Paul is saying that partial blindness, that veil over their hearts, is going to remain in place until the end of the world. But all Israel, the sons of God adopted by faith, who are the true seed of Abraham, shall be saved.

teachings.title: The Jews have no role in end times prophecy
teachings.summary: Jews have no role in the end times except destruction; the third temple is Christ and His body, and any rebuilt temple or sacrifices would be an abomination.
teachings.text:
One of the most helpful things in understanding end times Bible prophecy that I can recommend is forgetting everything you've ever heard about the Jews and their role in it. And then let the Bible speak.

Jews hold no role in in the end times aside from being utterly destroyed and cast into the lake of fire. They may help set up the antichrist and be betrayed so that the days of vengeance can occur. But other than that, they are meant to be a synagogue of Satan who will be made to see that God loved us who believe.

God isn't waiting on them to build a third temple. The third temple is Christ and the body of believers. Anything they build will not be called the Temple of God. It'll be an abomination.

God isn't waiting for them to return to doing sacrifices, and if they do, it too is an abomination. Blaspheming Jesus who is the only sacrifice.

teachings.title: The wine cup of God's fury on all nations
teachings.summary: God judges nations by their works while saving individuals by faith, and His fury poured on Judah and its neighbours foreshadows the judgment on end-times Babylon.
teachings.text:
In **Jeremiah 25** we see that the prophet has been preaching the word of God for 23 years, and he was not alone. Zephaniah and Habakkuk, and eventually Daniel and Ezekiel (after captivity began), are Jeremiah's contemporaries. The prophets of God trying to make strait the paths of Judah, while God uses His "servant," Babylon as the rod to lead them back to Him.

In chapter 25 we see the preaching of destruction and desolation of Judah laid out;

*Moreover I will take from them the voice of mirth, and the voice of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom, and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstones, and the light of the candle.*

But, the Lord says through Jeremiah that His wrath will also come to the other nations of the region, utterly destroying them as well. Babylon as an empire serving as God's tool to pour out His wrath. And Judah will be captive 70 years, saith the Lord.

But God also tells us that this desolation and destruction will come to all nations. That God will recompense them according to their deeds. God judges nations by works, even as He offers salvation to individuals by faith.

And so God gives the prophet an understanding that the wine of His fury will be poured out against them all. Both literally the nations of Egypt and Uz and Moab and Edom and the rest, and as we read on, God swears His vengeance on every nation, in that great and terrible day of the Lord.

Even as Isaiah preached. And as the revelation of Jesus Christ gave to John about the future nation with the spirit of Babylon upon it, whose destruction parallels with the destruction of Jerusalem in Jeremiah's day:

*And the light of a candle shall shine no more at all in thee; and the voice of the bridegroom and of the bride shall be heard no more at all in thee*.

Even as all hope for God's repentance is lost and Jerusalem and the other mighty nations of the time cannot escape the judgment that's upon them, God gives the hope that His wrath against His people will be short lived, and He will eventually turn that wrath against Babylon, the nation that has its spirit upon it in the end times.

teachings.title: Until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in
teachings.summary: Being grafted in is conditional on faith, and the fulness of the Gentiles simply means the harvest, when the Lord reaps at His coming before the wrath.
teachings.text:
*Behold therefore the goodness and severity of God: on them which fell, severity; but toward thee, goodness, if thou continue in his goodness: otherwise thou also shalt be cut off. And they also, if they abide not still in unbelief, shall be grafted in: for God is able to graft them in again*.

Again, note the conditional statements. IF we as a people continue in belief, we will remain in His goodness, and IF the Jew in unbelief repents, they will be graft back in. It is entirely conditioned on faith.

*For I would not, brethren, that ye should be ignorant of this mystery, lest ye should be wise in your own conceits; that blindness in part is happened to Israel, until the fulness of the Gentiles be come in.*

So many miss the point of this statement, which is a warning to the nations not to assume they deserve the blessings of grace through faith, as the unregenerate Jew had done. They get caught up in the "fullness of the Gentiles come in."

It is a curious turn of phrase that, because it points to a future event, many take and wrest with, trying to pinpoint what this means eschatologically. But it simply means when all those that are going to believe, have, the harvest comes. The day of the Lord, the rapture and the wrath. It's just a poetic way of saying this. Fullness being synonymous with the harvest. The fruit coming in. It isn't some esoteric hidden meaning.

Paul says that blindness *in part* (there's a remnant that believed, remember) has happened until the harvest of the nations is ready.

**Revelation 14:15**
*And another angel came out of the temple, crying with a loud voice to him that sat on the cloud, Thrust in thy sickle, and reap: for the time is come for thee to reap; for the harvest of the earth is ripe.*

God likens all of this to a vineyard throughout scripture. The spring feasts and fall feasts point to the first and second coming, the sowing and the harvest.

The fruits we produce are saved Christians we've led to Christ. The increase, the bounty of the harvest is God's. We are servants, husbandmen. He is the Lord of the harvest. And when the fullness of the Gentiles has come in, He will reap.

teachings.title: Shall not God avenge His own elect
teachings.summary: The parable of the unjust judge teaches us to pray always for the kingdom to come and for God's swift vengeance and wrath on the wicked.
teachings.text:
**Revelation 6:10**
*And they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?*

**Luke 18** opens continuing the teaching to Jesus' disciples on the coming of the day of the Lord, and He offers a parable that they understand to pray always for the kingdom to come, and not faint, not be worried or impatient. He gives an example of a man who is a judge, not God-fearing, not a respecter of persons, who when bothered repeatedly by a woman seeking him to avenge her against her adversary, decides to do it to avoid her constant bothering.

Jesus says if this unjust judge will do the right thing to avoid the widow's incessant pleading, how much more will God the Father avenge His elect in answer to their prayers?

When Jesus teaches us to pray, He says "Thy kingdom come" should be a part of it. We are told to pray for God's swift judgment, the day of the Lord, our salvation and redemption by the resurrection, and His glorious and righteous wrath being poured out on the earth and the wicked that remain.

Jesus assured us, He will come speedily. God, to Whom a thousand years is like a day to man, will not tarry. He will repay. Vengeance is His.

But, Jesus asks, *Nevertheless when the Son of man cometh, shall he find faith on the earth?*

teachings.title: Some shall not taste death: the transfiguration
teachings.summary: Jesus' saying that some would see the kingdom was fulfilled eight days later at the transfiguration, so lifting it out of context to support preterism is a failure to rightly divide.
teachings.text:
Now, Jesus ends all this by saying:

*But I tell you of a truth, there be some standing here, which shall not taste of death, till they see the kingdom of God.*

And immediately, Luke brings us to the transfiguration of Jesus on the mountain:

*And it came to pass about an eight days after these sayings, he took Peter and John and James, and went up into a mountain to pray.*

So, follow that. He tells them that some of them shall see Him come into His glory, glimpsing the kingdom of Heaven before they taste death, and it came to pass eight days later that three of them do just that.

This passage messes with people, where they come away with some kind of preterism or weird doctrines, because they don't rightly divide the word of God. They take a verse out of a larger narrative, stripped of context and then use their own foolish logic, try to make it make sense. Others who aren't familiar with the word pick up these errors and strange doctrines and repeat them. That's why we read all of it, in context, comparing scripture with scripture.

And so, Peter, James and John, the three Apostles who are closest to Jesus, witness Jesus transfigured in His glory, with Moses and Elijah who appear in glory. They are a witness to the Kingdom, out of due time.

It is often brushed over or minimized that Jesus was discussing His coming trials in Jerusalem with these great prophets of God, the culmination of God's will that these men preached in their day. What a conversation to be witness to, and add to that the understanding of the glory that awaits us in the Kingdom to come.

Peter, who always says the wrong thing, suggests building tabernacles for Jesus and these saints, as he attempts to process what they'd witnessed. And a cloud overtakes them and envelopes them, and the voice of the Father says to them "*This is my beloved Son: hear him.*"

Peter and the brothers, James and John are witnesses to the presence of God, Christ in His glory, with the glorified Old Testament saints with everlasting life, not in a vision, but present with them on the mountain. They've seen the Kingdom of God.

teachings.title: The Names of Christ in Revelation
teachings.summary: Revelation gives many names of Christ, including the Word of God, as He rides out after the marriage supper to the short battle of Armageddon.
teachings.text:
Alleluia! God be praised! The only appearance of the term, also spelled as hallelujah, (note Jah), transliterated from the Hebrew, but given us in Greek here, He is worthy of praise indeed.

Chapter 19 gives more detail to the triumphant beginning of the Kingdom of Heaven, Jesus Christ the Lord taking over the kingdoms of this earth, which we glimpsed in chapter 11;

*And the seventh angel sounded; and there were great voices in heaven, saying, The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever.*

*And the four and twenty elders, which sat before God on their seats, fell upon their faces, and worshipped God, Saying, We give thee thanks, O Lord God Almighty, which art, and wast, and art to come; because thou hast taken to thee thy great power, and hast reigned.*

Chapter 19 opens with a clear indication of the order of things we have read and John witnessed. Another "after these things," that we may know with certain faith that this is following the wrath, the same wrath as the trumpets and the same as the vials.

And again the inspired revelation gives us more names of Jesus, that we may worship Him, and in doing so makes us better understand the scriptures that precede **Revelation**.

I cribbed this list to put them in order and perspective:

1. Jesus Christ (Revelation1:1).
2. Faithful Witness (Revelation 1:5).
3. First Begotten Of The Dead (Revelation 1:5).
4. Prince Of The Kings Of The Earth (Revelation 1:5).
5. Alpha And Omega (Revelation 1:8-13).
6. First And Last (Revelation 1:8, 11, 13).
7. Son Of Man (Revelation 1;13).
8. He That Liveth And Was Dead (Revelation 1:13, 18).
9. He That Holdeth The Seven Stars (Revelation 2:1).
10. He Who Walketh Midst The Golden Candlesticks (Revelation 2:1).
11. He Who Hath The Sharp Sword With Two Edges (Revelation 2:12).
12. Son Of God (Revelation 2:18).
13. He Which Searches The Reins And Hearts (Revelation 2:23).
14. He That Hath The Seven Spirits Of God (Revelation 3:1).
15. He That Hath The Seven Stars (Revelation 3:1).
16. He That Is Holy And True (Revelation 3:7).
17. He That Hath The Key Of David (Revelation 3:7).
18. He That Openeth And No Man Shutteth (Revelation 3:7).
19. He That Shutteth And No Man Openeth (Revelation 3:7).
20. The Amen (Revelation 3:14).
21. The Faithful And True Witness (Revelation 3:14).
22. The Beginning Of The Creation Of God (Revelation 3:14).
23. Lord (Revelation 4:11).
24. Lion Of The Tribe Of Judah (Revelation 5:5,9).
25. The Root Of David (Revelation 5:5,9)
26. A Lamb As It Had Been Slain (Revelation 5:6-7).
27. The Lamb (Revelation 5:8-9).
28. Lord Of Lords (Revelation 17:14).
29. King Of Kings (Revelation 17:14).
30. Faithful And True (Revelation 19:11).
31. Rider Of The White Horse (Revelation 19:11).
32. The Word Of God (Revelation 19:13).
33. Christ (Revelation 20:4).
34. The Lord God Of The Holy Prophets (Revelation 22:6).
35. Beginning And The End (Revelation 22:13).
36. The Bright And Morning Star (Revelation 22:16).

Amen. And in chapter 19 we see further Jesus will come *with a name written, that no man knew, but he himself.*

The only time in the King James Bible that the Word of God is capitalized, making it a Name of Christ who is the Word made flesh. Faithful and true.

And the multitudes in Heaven, the saints called to the marriage supper, given wedding garments, white, the fine linen is the righteousness of saints. And a saint in heaven, a man redeemed in Christ, tells John to write;

*Blessed are they which are called unto the marriage supper of the Lamb. And he saith unto me, These are the true sayings of God.*

The wedding feast of **Matthew 22** is come. Alleluia.

And the Lord rides out on a white horse, followed by the army of the saints upon their own, as the beast and his prophet and the armies of those who worshipped the beast ride out to do battle against Him;

**Revelation 16:16**
*And he gathered them together into a place called in the Hebrew tongue Armageddon*

This is the battle of Armageddon. It is short lived.

teachings.title: The Fall of Babylon the Great City
teachings.summary: Babylon is destroyed last in the wrath, and the seat of Babylon is always some nation embodying its spirit, which today looks like the United States.
teachings.text:
And so, as the vials and trumps come to an end, the three and a half years of wrath poured out, special judgment is given against that great city, Babylon.

This is prophetic in the OT of both the actual Babylonian empire, but also the future empire represented in night visions and dreams interpreted by Daniel, and preached by the other prophets, which as we see in scripture, all speak of God's wrath followed by the coming of Christ and His kingdom.

When Jesus said that to Him gave all the prophets witness, we can see just how true that is.

And as we near the end of the judgement of the earth, and draw near to Christ's reign, the beast is readying the armies of man to resist Jesus and His saints. The earth has seen plagues and destruction since the day of the Lord. The sun and moon darkening and the rapture of the saints. Man has been in constant torment and fear from locusts from Hell, waters turned bitter and turned to blood. Fire from the sky and earthquakes. Giant hail. A relentless pouring out of God's wrath.

And at the end of all this, the representation of Babylon, the nation at the heart of the one world empire, is utterly destroyed in the span of an hour. Saved for last, God allows the people of the earth to see His righteous judgement upon it for the blood of the martyrs and the drunkenness of its fornication and abominations.

It is difficult not to see the United States as this city, especially given the merchants lament at the destruction of a great consumer nation. I believe that there is always a seat of Babylon, a country that embodies its spirit. Rome. London. The United States.

It is possible that should God be even more longsuffering than we reckon, it could be Hong Kong or some other nation that becomes the center for the beast. Every man feels like *surely these must be the final days. *I can't even imagine how they felt in WW2 for example. And yet even more horrors and evil were to come.

But reading this chapter, and the way it is described, it's difficult not to see things falling into place, faster and faster now. The beginning of sorrows feels imminent. And we long for the day when the angels sing out "*Rejoice over her, thou heaven, and ye holy apostles and prophets; for God hath avenged you on her."*

teachings.title: Can a Christian Take the Mark of the Beast?
teachings.summary: Answers an interview claiming saved Christians could take the mark or be punished in the Millennium, showing from Matthew 24, Revelation 3, 13 and 14 and 1 Thessalonians 5 that the saved are sealed and cannot be lost.
teachings.text:
In comments, someone posted a video by Kent Hovind, a disgraced former pastor who has some clout still in truther circles for his defense of biblical creation vs evolution. Though much of the rest of his doctrine is a mess., His personal life has left him unqualified to be a pastor, and demonstrated questionable character, but the debates he engages in with atheists over evolution draw in new followers all the time.

In this video that someone posted, Hovind gives time to a wicked heretic that I won't bother to name, who came to prominence in some evangelical circles nearly a decade ago, promoting a book based on the unbiblical idea that saved Christians could go to Hell during the Millennial Reign.

Often mocked as "Baptist purgatory doctrine," its promotion exposed many popular very-online pastors as false prophets.

Hovind begins by saying he "wonders what will happen if a Christian takes the mark" and starts the interview by saying to the viper who authored this heresy "I didn't want to believe it, but having read your book I can't say that it's wrong."

But the Bible can, and does.

In **Matthew 24:24** says of the end times;

*For there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect. *

It's not possible because the saved have the seal of the Holy Spirit upon us, and He lives within us.

The Bible says in Revelation chapter 13 that the false prophet, who will perform great wonders and deceive many to worship the beast and take the mark; *and cause that as many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed. And he causeth all, both small and great, rich and poor, free and bond, to receive a mark in their right hand, or in their foreheads:And that no man might buy or sell, save he that had the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of his name.*

Further, in chapter 14, the Bible says;

*And the third angel followed them, saying with a loud voice, If any man worship the beast and his image, and receive his mark in his forehead, or in his hand, The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation; and he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb: And the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever: and they have no rest day nor night, who worship the beast and his image, and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name.*

While in chapter 3 of Revelation, Christ promises the saved "*shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.*"

Those who are saved, whose names are in the book of life CANNOT take the mark. Again, chapter 13;* all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life.*

But further, irrespective of the mark, could backslidden Christians not be taken in rapture after the tribulation, and be present both for God's wrath and punished with Hell for a thousand years? Again, no.

**1 Thessalonians 5:9**
*For God hath not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ.*

We are saved by faith alone, not of works. If someone has believed, the Bible says, they shall not come into condemnation but have eternal life. This is the good news. This is the Gospel.

This twisted damnable heresy hinges on the behavior of Christians, their works, to save them from Hell, even if it is for "only" the thousand years of the Millennial Reign. It's wicked as Hell, as the viper who promoted it and all the false teachers who gave it an airing will find out.

teachings.title: Mystery Babylon, the mother of harlots
teachings.summary: The great whore on seven hills is Rome and its apostate church, with the false religions sprung from her as harlot daughters, drunk with the blood of the saints she martyred in a trail of blood, until the beast and his kingdom make war with the Lamb and are overcome.
teachings.text:
The Whore, Mystery Babylon the Great. Mother of harlots and abominations. Drunken with the blood of the saints she martyred. The golden cup filled of her filthy fornication and abominations.

*That great city which reigneth over the kings of the earth*.

Sitting upon 7 mountains.
Given power by kings to rule.
Decked in purple and scarlet, gold and precious stones and pearls.

Sitting upon many waters, which are peoples and multitudes and nations and tongues.

Who is this great whore? This mother of harlots? This city on 7 mountains, that sits on many waters? Who has martyred the saints of Jesus and committed fornication and blasphemy and other abominations against God?

The city on seven hills is Rome. Its whore, the false religion and apostate church of the Roman Catholics. The harlot daughters all the other false religions that have sprung from it. The Orthodox and the Protestant. All those calling themselves Christ's, professing themselves to be holy and true. But drunk in her fornications. Idolatry. Blasphemy. The abominations of her golden cup. The power of her political control, given by the kings that committed adultery with her. The murder of millions of believers, in a trail of blood, as this empire of miry clay and iron has conquered much of the earth.

In the end, the 7th empire as described by Daniel (we will look at Daniel 7 tomorrow, along with the destruction of Babylon), will give the beast power to reign and will promote the worship of the beast who was, is not and is again. The fatal wound and Satan bringing the antichrist back to life as the man of perdition, and installing him as the head of the final one world government and religion for a short space.

*These shall make war with the Lamb, and the Lamb shall overcome them: for he is Lord of lords, and King of kings: and they that are with him are called, and chosen, and faithful.*

teachings.title: Watch and Keep Thy Garments
teachings.summary: Christ comes as a thief only to the unwatchful, and anyone can know today they are saved by faith alone in His finished work.
teachings.text:
*Behold, I come as a thief. Blessed is he that watcheth, and keepeth his garments, lest he walk naked, and they see his shame.*

In the midst of the narrative Jesus reminds us of His oft repeated warning that to those who aren't watchful, who aren't sober, who aren't in the word and feeding the new man, but are in the world and feeding the old, he will come unexpectedly as a thief. But we are to watch and to know the signs and not be caught unaware. Not caught naked and ashamed, but clothed in the blood of the lamb. Dressed in white linen wedding garments, given to all who believe and overcome in Jesus. Who have the testimony of Christ.

Make sure you are not walking naked. Make certain you aren't appointed to wrath. The Bible says you can know you are saved today, by faith alone in the perfect works of Christ Jesus. A free gift, given by the grace and mercy of the living God. Justification by the blood. Jesus death as an atonement for our sin. And His resurrection the promise of God's word kept.

If you have not received the free gift of salvation or aren't certain that you will be with the saints in Heaven on the glorious day of the Lord's return, please take a moment to listen to this message; the Bible way to Heaven.

For faith comes by hearing and hearing by the word of God.

teachings.title: Revelation Tells the End Twice
teachings.summary: Comparing chapter 11 with 16 shows Revelation retells the end times twice, and preterism and other systems fail because they do not make the Bible the final authority.
teachings.text:
I want to add a quick note regarding the chronology of all of this, and how we can know that the first 11 chapters of Revelation and the second 11 chapters are retelling end times events.

If you look back in chapter 11, it's given to us that the kingdoms of this world have become Christ's.

*The kingdoms of this world are become the kingdoms of our Lord, and of his Christ; and he shall reign for ever and ever.*

But we see here in chapter 16, that the beast is still on his throne and is sending out evil spirits to convince all of the subordinate kings to gather their armies at Armageddon.

*And the fifth angel poured out his vial upon the seat of the beast; and his kingdom was full of darkness; and they gnawed their tongues for pain,*

If you have spent any time looking for answers in end times Bible prophecy, you will have come across a whole host of YouTube videos and internet posts that purport to give the chronology and explain the symbolism.

Of course, the dispensationalist version of events is the most prevalent today, but there's also the post-trib post-wrath version of end times Bible prophecy that's called the classical version. That conflates all of it and lists the seven seals and trumpets and vials as essentially the same thing, God's wrath. And that his people are not spared the wrath but forced to go through both the Great Tribulation and these plagues.

There are also those who say that the trumpets and the vials are the same judgments. Or that rather than happening concurrently happen 7 trump's and then 7 vials after the other. They don't rightly divide the word of God and will say that Revelation is all one continuous chronology.

But we can know simply by looking at scripture and comparing it to scripture precisely how it is divided, and how the order of events fits with other scripture such as the Olivet discourse given by Jesus in Matthew, Mark and Luke.

So when scripture in chapter 11 tells us that the Millennial reign is here, but then in chapter 16, we are told that the beast still has control of the kingdoms of the earth, it's easy to tell that this is simply a second run through of the events. Reiterating key points for our benefit.

It's also pretty clear, as we go through the book of Revelation, that the idea that this is already happened, that this was fulfilled in 70 AD (which is 20 years prior to the writing of Revelation), is all absurd. Anyone pushing that false doctrine cannot answer how it is that none of these great plagues and celestial events have ever taken place. Or explain how it is that Jesus is ruling and reigning with an iron rod today. That Satan is bound in Hell.

Far too many people who profess to be Christians settle on a theory or doctrine and then seek validation for it from other men. Rather than going to scripture and seeing what God has to say which dispels every false doctrine.

Those who don't treat the Bible as the final authority and the complete and perfect word of God will always be left struggling to come up with rationalizations to explain away the contradictions that arise from their false doctrines.

teachings.title: The Mark of the Beast and the Reprobate Mind
teachings.summary: Explains that taking the mark of the beast does not make a person reprobate; those who take it already were, as a free-will rejection of God and salvation.
teachings.text:
To clarify, taking the mark of the beast won't turn someone reprobate. It means they already were. The decision to worship the beast and take the mark might be the last straw that leads to God giving them up and giving them over to a reprobate mind, damning them. Just as with all reprobates it's a decision of the heart that does it. It's a free will choice to utterly reject God and salvation. The same as those who add to or take away from God's word to knowingly teach a false gospel or who blasphemed the Holy Ghost. It's not so much that the sin itself is unpardonable as it is an act that testifies to their reprobate mind. Their hardened heart.

They aren't made reprobate because they took the mark, they take the mark because they are reprobate.

Just as all who are saved who believe in their heart and confess with their mouth that Jesus is the Christ.

teachings.title: Miry Clay Mingled with Iron
teachings.summary: The miry clay mixed with iron may be false believers, chiefly the Catholic Church and her harlot daughters seeking political power.
teachings.text:
Delving a little bit deeper, we see Daniel talking about the feet of clay mixed with iron in the statue described in the dream. Traditionally in scripture the clay often represents believers. But here it is called miry clay, contaminated so as to not bind, mixed with iron which is the power of the state, the remnant of the Roman Empire's power.

This may represent false believers. Those who profess to be Christian but are not and have another gospel, primarily the Catholic Church.

Revelation, as we will see in chapter 17, will describe the whore of Babylon and her harlot daughters. From the description it clearly is the Roman Catholic Church, her harlot daughters the Protestants and various evangelical sects that have splintered off from the whore over the millennia. These churches claiming to be of Christ but seeking political power in the world.

 Miry clay mingled with iron.

And these 10 kingdoms of the final empire will be who gives the antichrist his power to rule.

teachings.title: Faith Over Fear in Great Tribulation
teachings.summary: Facing the beast's war on the saints, believers must trust God rather than their own preparations, love the brethren, and look to Him to provide in the wilderness.
teachings.text:
The moment many were waiting for, the prophecy of the beast, the antichrist and his false prophet. The mark and the number. 666.

The serpent, that old dragon Satan, gives power to the beast, who is mighty and given power to make war on the saints for 3.5 years. 42 months. He is described as having a head wound, and yet lives. A counterfeit Christ. Dead yet risen.

And as he makes war on the saints, those who fight with sword will die by sword, and those who bring others to captivity will be made captive. The beast, the antichrist will have the Uno reverse card and play it often. Testing the patience of the saints. Our faith in Jesus to save us out of Great Tribulation.

This is a hard saying. The Bible tells us again and again that we who keep watch, knowing the signs, staying in the word, won't be taken unawares. But we are expected to lean entirely on the Lord for our salvation from the beast. Not of ourselves.

Just like spiritual salvation. *And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony; and they loved not their lives unto the death.*

We are to trust God, and not love our own lives, even if it means death of the body. *But he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved.*

*And to wait for his Son from heaven, whom he raised from the dead, even Jesus, which delivered us from the wrath to come.*

We may die for the cause of Christ and for having His testimony. We may be cut off from buying and selling for refusing the mark of the beast, during a time we are told there will be great famines and pestilences. And all our preparing and stockpiling won't save us. But faith can.

And in that faith, in time of tribulation, whether the normal troubles that we face today, or that Great Tribulation to come, we are to love our brethren in the faith. Caring for one another. Sharing what we have with other saints.

*But as touching brotherly love ye need not that I write unto you: for ye yourselves are taught of God to love one another. And indeed ye do it toward all the brethren... but we beseech you, brethren, that ye increase more and more; And that ye study to be quiet, and to do your own business, and to work with your own hands, as we commanded you; That ye may walk honestly toward them that are without, and that ye may have lack of nothing.*

Having faith that there is a place provided us by God, that we may be nourished...

*And to the woman were given two wings of a great eagle, that she might fly into the wilderness, into her place, where she is nourished for a time, and times, and half a time, from the face of the serpent.*

It's easy to fall into fear at the prospect of being persecuted for our belief. At being cut off by famine and refusing to worship the beast. At being taken unawares and ill prepared. At facing death and starvation. At being cast out into the wilderness.

But there in the wilderness is where God provides. Manna from heaven. Quails in abundance. Locusts and wild honey. Fed by ravens. Water from flint. It takes but faith. The patience He demands of His people.

Faith over fear.

teachings.title: The Woman Is Not Modern Israel
teachings.summary: Scofield's teaching that the woman is Israel twists Joseph's dream to prop up a pre-trib rapture and Jewish kingdom, while Revelation mentions Jews only as persecutors.
teachings.text:
Just to reiterate, the Scofield view that the woman is Israel, in order to maintain the Dispensationalist view of end times Bible prophecy, is wrong. Nothing about it fits other than the 12 stars of the crown, the moon and sun, and even that is a stretch.

They use as proof text the story of Joseph and his dreams from **Genesis 37**:

*And he dreamed yet another dream, and told it his brethren, and said, Behold, I have dreamed a dream more; and, behold, the sun and the moon and the eleven stars made obeisance to me. And he told it to his father, and to his brethren: and his father rebuked him, and said unto him, What is this dream that thou hast dreamed? Shall I and thy mother and thy brethren indeed come to bow down ourselves to thee to the earth? And his brethren envied him; but his father observed the saying.*
